Indeed, a fool is not one who comes to this level, because if he understood and easily attained the laws of wisdom with clear knowledge called knowledge, he would not joke, because the fool is not a fool or a fool who disputes wisdom because of his own pleasure or because of desire. He only jokes and does not accept them because he does not understand them, although it is impossible for him to understand them because he must first accept them through faith and acceptance. And the joker when he sought wisdom and there was none, did not want to accept its laws because he joked about them, but the wise man accepted the laws of wisdom and understood one thing from another until he came to the general understanding:
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: "You go against a foolish man and do not know the words of knowledge - There is a difference between the fool and the scoundrel mentioned in the previous scripture:
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 1_Comment: * The joker does not joke about knowledge, only about wisdom, because there are no miracles about them, and they came to Kabbalah without clear knowledge, and if he had reached them with clear knowledge, he would not joke, only because he sought wisdom and did not find it, he did not come to the rule of reason, that he is after wisdom, because then knowledge would be easy in his eyes.
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 2_Comment: * But the fool is not a fool, and he has accepted the laws of wisdom, only lust has overcome him, and because the laws of wisdom oppose lust, therefore he will hate knowledge, as it is said (Proverbs 1:22): And fools hate knowledge, that is, even though he has accepted the laws of wisdom, and even though he is like the wise man until he knows their taste in knowledge, he will hate the knowledge that stands before Satan for him to his lust, as it is said (Proverbs 13:19): Lust becomes a hindrance to the soul and an abomination to fools who turn away from evil, as I explained there. Therefore he will hate knowledge, and will deceitfully cast a shadow over the laws of wisdom, so that he may have a blindfold on him in following the whims of his heart.
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 3_Comment: And if so, you, who knew my tongue of knowledge:
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 4_Comment: * You can go with the joker, because the joker will joke about wisdom, not about reason, as above;
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 5_Comment: * But not with a fool, who does not even accept reason.
text.13_Chapter, 6_Verse, 6_Comment: Therefore, go against a foolish man, for if you go with him without knowing the lips of knowledge, the knowledge that you have acquired, until you bring it out of your lips (which I have already explained that the lips indicate knowledge}, it will seem as if you did not know it, because by associating with a fool, you will learn from his actions to follow lust and confusion, as it is said (Proverbs 13:20): And he who shepherds fools will be destroyed, and you will be alienated from knowledge as if you did not know it at all.
text.13_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: "The wisdom of the naked man understands his way, and the folly of fools is deceit - it is drawn upward.
text.13_Chapter, 7_Verse, 1_Comment: He said that the foolishness of fools is a deception, because the fool is not a fool, because he is not truly satisfied with the ways of wisdom, but because he is restrained by the hand of desire that leads him astray, and the laws of wisdom and knowledge stand against him, he will act deceitfully and call upon folly, and say that he is satisfied with wisdom, and does not believe in it because of the sufficiency he has, and this is a deception, because truly a fool is not satisfied.
text.13_Chapter, 7_Verse, 2_Comment: And before this: The wisdom of the naked man understands his way - The naked man is not wise, meaning, he did not receive the laws of wisdom from the wise men to know all their paths, and yet he is not gullible, he is tempted by everything, because cunning enters into him, and his mind knows how to distinguish between good and evil and truth and falsehood, as it is said (Proverbs 1:4): To give guile to the simple. And cunning will teach him to understand his way, so that he will not follow a path that he is unsure of and does not know whether it is good or bad, but will only strive to understand with his mind the essence of his way, and this is his wisdom, that although he did not receive all the laws of wisdom to know all the paths according to the Kabbalah from the wise men, in all this, in the particular path that he walks, he will pay attention to understanding it, and from this he will arrive at wisdom in some details. And this is the wisdom of the naked man.
text.13_Chapter, 7_Verse, 3_Comment: And if so, how can the fool, who is not gullible, follow the path of foolishness that he doubts?! Only this foolishness is truly deceitful, not real.
text.13_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: The wicked will be guilty, the counsellor is the one who stands between two people to reveal the ideas of one to the other who does not understand his language and his secrets, as if he had advised between them, and his speech Between the wicked will be guilty and between the righteous will be willing, R"l Although the wicked are the ones who are content and deny the laws of wisdom and absolutely oppose it (not like the fools who do this deceitfully to produce their desires), and the upright are the opposite. The wicked are those whose hearts are upright in the ways of understanding and attain the truth, and the ways of wisdom are secure and fortified in their hearts, the parroting of their thoughts and the secrets of their hearts will be recognized, because the wicked are guilty in their souls (the fence of the guilty is the one who recognizes that he is liable to punishment for his actions) that the heart that feels will feel about his actions whether good or bad, and the heart of the wicked will feel that he is liable to punishment, and his inner soul will be bitter about his actions, and the heart of the upright will rejoice and feel that his actions are desirable, and this is the counsellor between them to reveal mysteries Their secrets, because Hashem will advise among the wicked, and will reveal the secrets of their hearts that feel that they deserve punishment, and they do not do their deeds with joy because their hearts will not rest, And among the upright in will He will advise and reveal the secrets of their thoughts, who feel that their deeds are pleasing and rejoice in their deeds:
text.13_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: The heart knows the bitterness of its soul, explains that this feeling lies in the innermost heart and soul of a person. The heart of the wicked knows the bitterness of its soul, for its inner soul is bitter to it and has no rest because that soul is to blame and is moved by it. Likewise, No outsider will interfere with the joy of the heart of the upright, because it is an internal matter and a very unknown feeling:
text.13_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the righteous will flourish. This feeling will foretell to him what his end will be. The heart knows the bitterness of its soul and recognizes that the house of the wicked will be destroyed. Even though his house is built with strength, in 27 it will end up being destroyed and will not stand. And in its joy, the righteous will recognize that the tent of the righteous will flourish. The righteous, even though they do not have a permanent home, only a temporary tent, and it has not yet sprouted or grown, in 27 it will flourish and be very proud, and this is an inner feeling that both the wicked and the righteous will feel in him:
text.13_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: There is a straight path before a man, it is said about the above, that although sometimes the path of the wicked may be better in his eyes, because the path of the wicked seems straight at first, against the path of wisdom, which at its beginning seems to go over thorns and briers, because one must fight against the desires and states of the soul that tend to evil, as the saying goes (Lema' 12:16) The path of the wicked is straight in his eyes, yet its end is the way of death, whereas the path of wisdom begins with thorns and ends with a plain:
text.13_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: Even in laughter, the heart will ache, and therefore, even though you see on the face of the unfortunate one that he is laughing, and the hour is right for him, the heart will ache because the heart knows the bitterness of its soul and feels that in the end, joy is sorrow, and in the end it knows that joy is truly sorrow, because it will walk the path of death, and there is a difference between laughter and joy. The laughter is seen only in its exterior, and the joy is in the heart, and there is a crying and laughing person who cries in his heart and laughs with his mouth, as it is said about Rabbi Akiva who cried and laughed, and may Hashem have mercy on him who laughs and whose heart is in pain:
text.13_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: A heart will be satisfied with his ways, and a good man will be above him. The heart will be satisfied, R"L. He whose heart withdraws, R"L. His heart does not agree with his actions because he feels that his way is not good, as the saying goes: A heart knows the bitterness of its soul, even in laughter the heart will be pained, nevertheless he will be satisfied with his ways. Another who walks in the ways of death will be satisfied with his ways and receive his punishment, and therefore A good man will withdraw A good man will withdraw from him, not only will his heart withdraw, but his whole being will withdraw and turn away from him and not do as he did:
text.13_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: "A fool will believe everything, but a fool will understand what is right - After speaking of the fool and the wretch, who themselves are deceived by their own hearts, and are not sure of their path, he says that in contrast to this, the fool, who is defined as someone who is devoid of understanding and is deceived like a deceived dove, has no heart, he believes everything, whether the words of the fool or the words of the wretch, without discerning at all, and his heart is not deceived at all.
text.13_Chapter, 14_Verse, 1_Comment: But the naked man, who has become gullible, and has a cunning heart to examine everything, will not be deceived, he will only understand what is beneficial to his own good and spiritual success, as it is said (Proverbs 14:8): The wisdom of the naked man - he understands his way, (Proverbs 13:15): Every naked man acts with knowledge.
text.13_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: "A wise man should fear and shun evil" - Wisdom needs morality, meaning, since in the paths of morality there are two paths in each person, one path is wisdom and its opposite is folly, and the heart's inclination tends to evil, because the images that were planted in his heart from the time of his birth tend to lust and the pleasures of the flesh and are opposite to the paths of wisdom. Behold, when the inclination of his heart tempts him to deviate from the paths of wisdom, he easily listens to the advice of inclination, and he needs something in which he will chasten the forces of his soul lest they go beyond the boundaries of wisdom. And this morality is the fear of Hashem, who knows that a great king stands over him and sees his actions, and he becomes dry and afraid of doing anything against his will, and therefore (Psalms 111:10): "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem," which is a condition for wisdom and the gateway to it.
text.13_Chapter, 15_Verse, 2_Comment: * The wise man, by fearing the Lord, thereby turns away from evil, and does not deviate from the counsel of wisdom, for the one who abstains will torment his soul beyond its limits.
text.13_Chapter, 15_Verse, 3_Comment: * But the fool transgresses and crosses the boundaries of morality and wisdom, and is confident, that confidence is the opposite of fear, because he does not fear the fear of Hashem and the glory of His genius.
text.13_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: A short-tempered person will commit a crime, and a man of scheming will hate, from the path of wisdom to prolong his anger and not to take revenge and quarrel immediately, as the saying goes: "A long-tempered person is wise, but a short-tempered person brings forth a crime." And this is from the path of wisdom, and wisdom will also require, as the saying goes: "Any person who prolongs his anger, because if he quarrels with his friend or takes revenge on him, he quarrels with him and despises him, and his enemy will turn on his head. Therefore, a man of wisdom will keep silent (ibid. 11:12). And whoever is short-tempered will commit a crime, he is satisfied with the paths of understanding and reason. There are short-tempered and short-tempered people, and short-tempered people will also be depicted in someone who is long-tempered, because the nose is the external nose, and the spirit is what brings up the images on the heart. And whoever is short-tempered will not be able to calm his spirit and will bring up the images of revenge and hatred on his heart. And even if he prolongs his anger and does not do evil openly, he will keep his hatred in his heart for a while. It is a commandment, and although it is not against the ways of reason and intellect, it is against the laws of wisdom, which commands that one should not raise these evil images in his mind upon his heart, only to humiliate them, and to raise in their place the images of suffering and mercy and humility and forgiveness, and he is a curse and a doubt in the ways of wisdom, and Hashem forbid there is a curse and a short-tempered person raises a curse, because although he does not commit a curse, he raises it from the depths of the soul upon the heart, but he is short-tempered and takes revenge immediately in practice, he commits a curse in action, and a man of schemes, is called one who plots deep thoughts for evil, as it is written, "He who plots evil shall be called a man of schemes," and although he also prolongs it because he lies in wait and plots to bring him down in a net, he is hated because he who lies in secret to strike his neighbor is hated by all:
text.13_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: The foolish have inherited a curse, I have already said that the foolish will believe everything, and he is more beautiful than the fools and the foolish, like a deceived dove, and he receives the curse and the suffocation by way of inheritance, like an heir who inherits from others, so he receives from the foolish and does not know what and does not discern at all, but the naked are the opposite of the foolish. They examine everything and do nothing but know well what and why he will do it, and although they are not wise and intelligent, they will crown themselves with knowledge, knowledge is a crown on their head, and those who are crowned will not do anything without knowledge, as stated above:
text.13_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: The wicked bow before the good, he said, although the evil opposes the good and the wicked oppose the righteous, in all this, when the evil comes before the good, he will speak before him and submit to him, and likewise the wicked when they come to the gates of a righteous man, they bow before him, and the nature of evil is such that it will not stand before the good, just as darkness will not stand before the light:
text.13_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: (22-21) Even a rich man will hate his neighbor, a sinner will despise his neighbor, he said, although it is nature for love to be between like-minded people, we have seen the opposite, that a rich man will hate a rich man, and love the rich man, and this is against the laws of wisdom, which require loving humility and humiliation, showing mercy and showing favor to the humble, and hating pride, and this hates a rich man because he is poor and oppressed, Azza He who despises his neighbor a rich man is a sinner, for sin is what transgresses the laws of wisdom, and the one who is gifted with humility is for the happiness of the soul, which will learn to love humility and hate pride:
text.13_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: Will not those who plant evil go astray? The planter is one who plans to do something in silence without letting anyone know. And those who plant evil will go astray. Because the one who strays from the path, in a place where they see, will be guided by those who pass by on the straight path. But those who plant evil in secret tend from the path of wisdom to a crooked path. And will they not always go astray because no one sees the path leading to them. But those who plant good and hide their deeds, this comes from the side of kindness and truth. Because the one who does good openly expects reward, or honor and glory, and the one who does good to his fellow man in secret does not expect to be rewarded. And this is from the side of the fact that kindness and truth have prevailed in his soul, which is an act of kindness for which there is no reward:
text.13_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: In every sorrow, it is permissible and speaking with the lips is only for a shortage, the Sages have already said (Berakhot 7) Agrah Debi Tamia Shtikuta, R. L., that for every evil that comes upon a person, one should be saddened in his heart, and remember that it came upon him through his sins, and reflect on repentance in his heart, which is the mourning and mourning for the dead, and it is good to go to a house of mourning and let the living give to his heart, until in every sorrow, he will be permitted and rewarded, and 27 in his heart, but if he expresses it with his lips it is a way of resentment that he is resentful that he was treated this way, and this will be for a shortage, as in the words of Aaron, and he received a reward for his silence, etc.:
text.13_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 14:24): The crown of the wise is their wealth - The crown that the wise wear as a sign of their wisdom is their wealth, because the possession of wisdom is true possession, and they are the truly rich, because it is more precious than pearls.
text.13_Chapter, 23_Verse, 1_Comment: It should also be interpreted: The wealth of the wise is their crown, meaning, that by means of wisdom they withdraw from the lusts of the world and rejoice in their lot, which is true wealth - one who does not covet and lacks nothing for his soul, because the rich man who covets and whose eye is never satisfied with wealth is the truly poor.
text.13_Chapter, 23_Verse, 2_Comment: The folly of fools is folly - It has already been explained (in verse 8) that the folly of fools is deceit, because the fool is not a fool, and he knows the laws of wisdom, only because of his lust he is forced to deny the laws of wisdom and interpret folly, as it is said (Proverbs 13:16): And a fool will spread folly, that he may have a covering for his eyes, he will spread the veil of folly over wisdom to blind her eyes, and he is truly deceitful, because he himself knows that the laws of wisdom are true, and therefore the foolishness of the fool and his doubts are folly and doubt, because folly is not certain to him, only folly, meaning doubt.
text.13_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: Saving souls to truth, R"l. Whoever comes and bears true testimony before the Lord and thus saves souls who were condemned to death by false witnesses, is the one who saves souls in truth. But if he utters lies The one who saves souls if he comes to save the condemned through false words, (and already in my Barati (P. 5) that he apprehended uttering lies, that he cannot say a clear lie, only a lie that will seem to be true for its time, and said uttering it is an incomplete word) this does not save souls because it is deception and deceit, and he will not be called by the name of the purpose a savior of souls only if he comes through truth and not through deceit:
text.13_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 14:26): In the fear of the Lord one finds strength - wisdom itself, without the fear of the Lord, does not exist, as the Sages said (Mishnah, Tractate Avot): Whoever fears his sin before his wisdom - his wisdom exists, etc., and they said (Mishnah, Tractate Avot): If there is no fear - there is no wisdom, because even if he knows the laws of wisdom, are not there pitfalls all around him in the depths of the soul, desires and evil images, and he will easily deviate from its laws, only the fear of the Lord will restrain the powers of the soul from morality, so that he will never deviate from the laws of wisdom. Therefore, the one who trusts in the laws of wisdom that he has gathered in his soul is not a strong confidence, because this fortress will easily be conquered by the city's besiegers who have built great traps against it, but the one whose fear of his sin precedes wisdom has the refuge of strength, and his wisdom exists, until his children too will have Shelter, as it is said (Psalms 25:12): Who is the man who fears the Lord... and his seed will inherit the land, (Psalms 121:1): Blessed is the man who fears the Lord... his seed will be mighty in the land.
text.13_Chapter, 26_Verse, 0_Comment: The fear of Hashem is a source of life to avoid the pitfalls of death. The path of wisdom is the path of life, but around it are pitfalls of death. It is the stronghold of desire and lust that want to throw the soul into the path of death. Even though one knows the laws of wisdom, he is not sure that the lurker sitting in the room will not trap him in his traps. However, through fear, the powers of the soul will be tormented (as in the previous scripture). There is the source of life, from whose waters he will live eternal life and avoid the pitfalls of death. Fear without Torah and wisdom is also not beneficial, because he does not know what to do and what is the path of wisdom, as it is said: "If there is no wisdom, there is no fear." Therefore, it was said above (13:14) The law of a wise man is a source of life to avoid the pitfalls of death:
text.13_Chapter, 27_Verse, 0_Comment: In the majority of the people, the king's honor and the nation's honor are due to the majority of the people. The community that has a king is called a people (which is the difference between a gentile and a people), and the community that has a special religion is called a nation. Counts are the ministers of advice. There is a difference between a count and an advisor. The advisors are in matters of state and their advice is open, while the counts are in matters of secrecy and under their command are all matters of religion and law, as it is said, "And the counts shall legislate justice." The king's honor is due to the majority of the people. There is a difference between grandeur and honor, for honor is the external grandeur in everything according to our interests, and according to the majority of the people, the king's honor will increase. But the ratio, who is in charge of religious laws, even when there is a people or nation that does not have the knowledge of the 13th , is due to the majority of the people, because he will not act on anything:
text.13_Chapter, 28_Verse, 0_Comment: A long-suffering man, full of wisdom and short-tempered, raises a burden, I have already explained above that being long-suffering and not taking immediate revenge is the opposite of the laws of wisdom. And there is a long-suffering man and short-tempered man, meaning that his heart will not be quiet and his spirit will immediately rise up to the images of revenge at any time, and he is a burden against the laws of wisdom and he raises the burden from the depths of the soul to the outside, and I have already explained this in verse 17:
text.13_Chapter, 29_Verse, 0_Comment: The life of the flesh is a healing heart, translated above in the Mishnah and the short-tempered Miriam Olat, says one who raises the images of envy that envies his honor on the heart. In addition to the Olat against wisdom, he corrupts another A.A. The heart heals the life of the flesh, that the life of the flesh and its healing if its strength weakens, depends on the heart, when the heart is brave and strong, it sends its springs into rivers, they run in a flood through the arteries and water the flesh and revive it. Therefore, one who raises envy to the heart not only consumes the flesh, but also rots the bones, and consumes his body, and as the Mishnah says, "Guard your heart from every guard, for from it are the results of life:"
text.13_Chapter, 30_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 14:3): The oppressor of the poor is a disgrace to his maker - Hashem did not create man for his own harm, only for his own good, and for every creature He created - He prepared food for it, and He prepared the tools with which it would hunt and prepare its food, and this is from the honor of the Creator, who created everything for their benefit and to live a life of refinement and goodness. Indeed, man, whose sustenance is difficult to obtain, and there are poor and needy people who cannot obtain their sustenance, prepared by nature that man would help his fellow man, as it is said (Proverbs 22:2): The rich and the poor meet together, the Lord makes them both:
text.13_Chapter, 30_Verse, 1_Comment: * That the poor should engage in work for the rich who has a lot of work and needs workers,
text.13_Chapter, 30_Verse, 2_Comment: * And the poor will receive charity by way of a free gift.
text.13_Chapter, 30_Verse, 4_Comment: * He oppresses the "poor" and does not give him his wages, despite the one who made him, as if he created him for his own harm and did not provide him with his prey and his life in which to exist, and this is a great disgrace to the one who made him, to make an animal and not provide it with its needs, and they have already said that whoever gives me life - will give me food.
text.13_Chapter, 30_Verse, 5_Comment: * And the one who "gives a poor man a free gift (because the poor man cannot engage in labor) honors the one who made it, for this is His glory, who created the rich and the poor, that the rich give charity and fulfill the commandments of Hashem, which is the glory of Hashem, who created nothing in vain.
text.13_Chapter, 31_Verse, 0_Comment: In his evil he will be rejected, the wicked man, even when he is on high, will be rejected from his place to a pit of corruption, and this rejection will be in his evil, his own evil will be rejected from his place, and the righteous man is not alone in not being rejected while he is alive. For even in his death he takes refuge in the Lord and in the shadow of His wings:
text.13_Chapter, 32_Verse, 0_Comment: In the heart of the wise, wisdom will rest. There is a difference between the wise and the unwise. The wise received the laws of wisdom from his masters and did not understand their meaning. When wisdom comes into his heart and he keeps its laws, behold, when the images of lust and folly that oppose the laws of wisdom also come, a heavy battle will arise in his heart (which is the ruling force within him), and the wisdom that is in his heart has an internal battle with the evil images of the heart and has no rest. But the wise is the one who understands a thing from a thing, and he understands the laws of wisdom with his intelligence, and understands how to subdue the desires of the heart that oppose it, and the arms of reason and understanding will stand as a shield for it. And wisdom will rest, R"l 1"l rest from its enemies, but the fools in whom lust and passion prevail and drive wisdom out of the heart will not be found in their hearts. Only it will be known among them that they will use it for evil and that they will turn away from the path of wisdom, and already in my book The fool is not a fool or a fool, for he knows the laws of wisdom and they are within him, only not in his heart, for in his heart desire and inclination will reign and drive wisdom from ruling with its powers:
text.13_Chapter, 33_Verse, 0_Comment: Justice elevates a nation, and kindness to nations is sin. There is a difference between a nation and a nation, as the nation is the nation with a special religion, and the people with a king, and the nation is the collective community alone, which has neither a king nor a special religion. In all this, justice elevates it. When those who follow the path of justice rise from their lowliness and attain honor, and even the nations, although they have a religion, sin is the deviation from the path of wisdom, and justice is for them kindness, which is the greatest disgrace.
text.13_Chapter, 34_Verse, 0_Comment: <b>A king's will for a wise servant, and his transgression will be shameful. The wise one is the one who is quick in his work and acts wisely to look to the end, and the shameful one is the one who is slow and does not look to the end. And when they become slaves to a king whose service is the service of all, he will fulfill his will for the wise one, and because of the shameful one, a transgression will be fulfilled for all his servants, which is a boundary of transgression that is also felt by the sinless one, and this is the moral of the matter, as it is said: A man will always see the world as half righteous and half guilty. He deserves to be judged, and the whole world as a weight of merit, because through the wise servant, a will will come from the Supreme King, and if he does not deserve to be judged, he will judge and the whole world, etc., until a transgression is fulfilled for the whole world:
text.14_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: A soft answer will return anger, but a word of bitterness will raise anger. There is a difference between anger and bitterness, as bitterness is the anger that is kept in the heart with warmth and a burning fire, and bitterness is the external foam, the bitterness is visible and revealed, not the anger, and in 27 the anger is greater than the anger, because the anger when it is without inner anger is not so cruel, like a father who is angry with his son and hits him with the anger, but in his heart he loves him, he said that when he answers with a soft answer, the inner anger will also return and the enemy will return to loving him, but the matter is bitterness that he will answer with something to grieve the speaker, not only will he not return anger, but the external anger will also rise to take revenge on him immediately, because the raising of the anger is the revenge, just as the Lord rose up against them and killed them in their fat:
text.14_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: The tongue of the wise will excel knowledge, but the mouth of fools will utter folly. I have already explained that knowledge falls on things that are understood by the senses, or that are clear knowledge as if they were understood by the senses, and wisdom is accepted and has no clear examples for it and the senses will not grasp it, and in 27 The tongue of the wise will excel knowledge, the language indicates intelligent speech, if they speak wisely in intelligent speech, their intelligence will become clear in their example and they will return to the level of knowledge, and it was already said above that the wise will conceal knowledge, meaning that they will not reveal it to everyone except to the intelligent, with whom they will speak in the language that the speech indicates is superior to understanding, and this language will excel knowledge, however, when they speak in external language, they will make a golden garland around it and conceal their words, for (v. 7) The tongue of the wise will scatter knowledge, but the fool, who, although he has received the laws of wisdom, will be overcome by desire and will therefore cast doubts on the laws The wisdom that is called folly, he will not speak with the tongue and language that are the speech of reason and knowledge, because a fool will not understand this, only with his mouth will he express folly and sufficiency, and I have already written that the mouth implies speech in wisdom, and in contrast to this he will speak folly which is opposition to wisdom, and the source of folly is in his mouth not in his heart because the folly of fools is deceitful (above 15:8) folly of fools (ibid. 24) whose heart is not satisfied only with the source of folly is in his mouth as above:
text.14_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: The eyes of Hashem are everywhere, watching the evil and the good, R"l. Although many believe that providence extends beyond reason and after the "Maat", and although we have found that Hashem will hide His face from evil and will not be able to look at labor, 27 know that the eyes of Hashem are everywhere. R"l. Although according to the picture we draw that looks from His holy place or from a place or to a place prepared for private providence, we say that this place and this person are special to the world of providence, and this place and the person will hide his face from it and not look at them. But according to the view that all of creation is the eyes of Hashem, and everything was prepared in such a way that nothing is left to chance, and all of nature and the process and the outcome are filled with eyes that are the messengers of Providence that look and observe everything that is done, and there is no darkness and no shadows where evildoers can hide, because the eyes stand around them everywhere, and they watch between the bad and the good and everything is ready for calculation, and the watcher is the one who watches the future to come, and so these eyes, which are the eyes of Providence, will watch the future between the bad and the good, and all according to the Providence that fills all places:
text.14_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: Healing the tongue is a tree of life and distorting it is a fracture in the spirit, it is illustrated that the distortion of the tongue R"t. The tongue that deviates from the path of wisdom and speaks to the high and gossip (and when it is interpreted in the understanding that it is a fence of mere tongue which is the intellectual speech) is a fracture in the spirit, R"t. Since speech is the bones of man, he who distorts the tongue comes from an internal fracture rooted in the spirit of man, whose spirit is broken and sick and is not whole, because what spoils the strength of the animal soul is a fracture in the animal soul which is not as dangerous as a fracture in the spirit, however the tree of life is a cure for the diseases of the tongue, which is the business of the Torah and wisdom which is a tree of life for those who hold it, will heal the tongue, like medicinal trees that cure every disease, and whoever does not use this medicine and by tempting the tongue will not eat from the tree of life, only from the tree of knowledge Good and evil that death brought into the world by the first possessor of the tongue, which is the serpent (as in, if the serpent bites without a charm, what advantage does the possessor of the tongue have), and he who distorts with his tongue, this is a sign that his inner spirit has been broken and he has an evil spirit:
text.14_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: Woe to him who despises the discipline of his father and heeds the reproof of his elders, the discipline is built on fear, which disciplines the powers of his soul by reminding him of the punishments that come to one who deviates from the path of wisdom, and he needs knowledge, who knows that there is a watcher who rewards and punishes and fears Him, and in this he will take discipline, as it is said (12:1) He who loves discipline loves knowledge, and behold the fool knows the laws of wisdom, only that lust overcomes him, even though he does not accept discipline in 27, he will not despise it in his heart, because if it were not for lust and desire, he would accept discipline and walk in the laws of wisdom, but the woe to him who is content with everything and does not love knowledge, he will despise the discipline in his heart because he does not believe at all in Hashem's punishments and in His providence, and behold the reproof is built on the power of reason, which shows him, according to reason, the benefit and goodness of wisdom, and this the woeful one will not despise, as long as he is willing to accept something of wisdom, only The ignorant, who is the animal who does not understand anything and has no power of reason at all, as the saying goes, and hates reproof, is ignorant (ibid.). The opposite of the ignorant and gullible is the one who has entered into his heart cunningness, so that he begins to distinguish between good and evil, and the one who heeds reproof emerges from ignorance into cunningness:
text.14_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: The house of a righteous man is good and strong, good is the word of the existing and strong. And he has already said that the house of the righteous will stand, because his house is built firmly on the machinery of righteousness, and this is the word of the existing and strong, indeed if the fruit of the wicked is brought into the house, that he may share with the wicked and he brings there his fruit which is robbery and plunder, the house will be disturbed. And everything will be destroyed in a bad matter, as the saying goes: He who disturbs his house will inherit a wind, because when you associate with the wicked, the Lord will break your works. And in the parable of the royal house, he is the one who builds the house of his soul on the machinery of righteousness, and this is the 11th 11th 12th 13th 14th 15th 16th 17th 18th 19th 20th 21st 22nd 23rd 24th 25th 26th 27th 28th 29
text.14_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: The lips of the wise will pour out knowledge, but the hearts of fools will not. I have already written (verse 2) Sha'ar"l that the wise will put a garland around knowledge to protect it from the fools whose mouths will utter folly and deceit, as the saying goes: "The wise will hide knowledge as the saying goes." Indeed, fools, although they utter folly with their mouths, will turn away knowledge, and so will their lips, as the saying goes: "Go against a fool and do not know the lips of knowledge." Their hearts are not like that, for in their hearts they know the laws of wisdom, only that their eyes may be opened to them, and their hearts do not stand firm and firm, for they will move like foam on the surface of the water.
text.14_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Hashem - meaning, the main thing about the sacrifice is not the sacrifice itself, only the intention that shows that one repents of one's sins, or that with the sacrifice one confesses and prays to Hashem by shedding one's soul along with the shedding of the blood of the sacrifice. But the wicked, who does not abandon his wickedness and thinks of appeasing himself with the sacrifice itself, is an abomination to Hashem.
text.14_Chapter, 7_Verse, 1_Comment: But the righteous do not need sacrifice, only prayer, which is His will, and their prayer will be heard even without sacrifice.
text.14_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: The path of the wicked is abominable to Hashem. Just as in a sterile good deed, it is the intention, not the deed itself, that contradicts His intention. Likewise, in wickedness, apart from Hashem hating the wicked, which is the evil action, the path of the wicked one in which he approaches the wicked is also abominable to Him, for he follows the path of pride, revenge, and cruelty, and his soul is evil about it. And this is more abominable than the deed itself, because it grows from the evil of the soul's nature, which is more difficult than the evil of the deed, which is in the action of the body, as Maimonides says: "The thoughts of a transgression are harder than the transgression, and the pursuit of righteousness, even though he has not achieved righteousness, he only pursues it out of his great desire for it and the intention of his heart, him will be loved by Hashem, because the main thing for him is the mental intention:
text.14_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: Bad morals for leaving a place. There is good morals and bad morals. Good morals frighten him with the punishment that will come upon the wicked, and in this he torments his soul's strength lest he depart from the good path out of fear for the future. And bad morals are those that bring upon him severe and bitter torments, and this is what Hashem will do to the one who leaves a place. He who has already walked the path of wisdom and leaves and changes and interprets, torments him with severe torments. And if a person sees that torments are coming upon him, he will scrutinize his actions or be hung up on nullifying the Torah, and through bad morals he will be rebuked, meaning that he is rebuked and shown according to reason how Hashem has rewarded him for his actions. And he will not return to the pit again, and if he loves rebuke, he will return and be healed of his torments. And if he hates rebuke, he will die through bad morals:
text.14_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: Sheol and Abaddon are against Hashem, against those who say that Hashem does not know the thoughts of men, whether because they are deep and very hidden within a person and a deep heart, or because of their changeability that the river of thoughts always flows through, and may Hashem renew the multitude of knowledge and change of knowledge, and the like from the questions of the philosophers, he says, Sheol, which is deeper and more hidden than the heart, and Abaddon, which is the material substance that always changes its forms and takes on another form without ceasing, in all this he is against Hashem and knows its depths and changes, even though He knows the hearts of men:
text.14_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: A fool will not love a fool who has been proven to him. The fool is one who jokes about the laws of wisdom and morality, because they cannot be clarified to him by the evidence of reason, but he cannot joke about the rebuke that he and the power of reason can do, only because he hates rebuke and is guarded against it. And Hashem forbid, a fool will be removed, taking away his disgrace and rebuking the wicked for his own sake. But the one who rebukes a fool with evidence will not be relieved because he has submitted to the power of reason, only because he hates the one who rebukes and is therefore guarded against the reign of the wise. He is not guarded against morality, because he jokes, only because of the rebuke, and because he does not love rebuke, therefore he will not go to the wise. And I have already explained in the Torah, the Holy Ones, 33:43, that there is a difference between a person who is followed by You rebuke him about a private matter, and do not rebuke a liar, lest he hate you. And when he does not rebuke him about a private matter, he does not hate you, and he does not love rebuke.
text.14_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: A joyful heart will make a good face, the joy of the heart and its sadness will be in several ways, and here he is speaking of a heart that is joyful in worldly affairs, as the saying goes, "And my heart rejoices in all my labors," and he is one who does not grieve over his sins and the lack of his talent in the perfection of his soul, because his heart rejoices in his success, and he will only make a good face, because the joy of the heart is evident on the face, but it will not make the spirit better with this, because the spirit includes all the inner powers of the soul, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of knowledge and the fear of Hashem, and sometimes the heart is happy and the spirit is downcast, because the spirit is low and rebellious and downcast because it is concerned with the pleasures of this world and its joy alone, but with sadness of heart (it will make) a downcast spirit, by making him grieve over his spiritual status, his spirit will be exalted and will lift him up, and this is better than making a good face, and see my commentary on the verse A joyful heart will make a good face:
text.14_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise heart seeks knowledge, I have already explained that the wise is the one who understands a thing from a thing, and therefore comes to the general knowledge that even in the laws of wisdom he will understand their meaning and know knowledge in them, as the saying goes (10:13) On the lips of the wise will be found wisdom, indeed knowledge will not be easily attained only after much request and observation, and the heart, which is the governing force when it comes to leading in the ways of wisdom, will seek to know its meanings and secrets, but the fool, who does not abandon wisdom because of the error that the fool is not as foolish as above, only because of his desire, his heart will not seek wisdom and sufficiency like the fool who seeks wisdom, may Hashem labor to find arguments about the ways of wisdom in the wonders of misleading philosophers, not so the fool, because the wisdom of fools is deceptive like the scribe there, only the face of fools will see wisdom, for although his heart will not see wisdom, his face will see it, the face depicts the intention that he sets his face towards, After turning his face to the path of desire, he will graze a flock of sheep to hide it from his face, and he will find the flock standing before him like a flock of sheep, and he is the shepherd:
text.14_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 15:15): All the days of the poor are evil - Interpreting, that (Proverbs 15:14): In the face of fools folly will feed, he is discontented with what he sees before him, and he asks: Have we not seen that "all the days of the poor are evil"?! The poor, who is afflicted because he obeys the laws of the Torah, nevertheless his days are always evil, and he who always feasts is good-hearted, and from this he proves that there is no reward for walking wisely.
text.14_Chapter, 14_Verse, 1_Comment: But a wise heart will seek knowledge, and will answer him thus:
text.14_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: A little in the fear of the Lord is better. A little is given to the poor because he is engaged in the fear of the Lord and walks the path of perfection. It is better than one who gives a great treasure to another who finds turmoil in it, because he will destroy his soul and spiritual happiness, and he will bear the burden of his own sin:
text.14_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: Better is a meal of vegetables and love than a manger bull and hatred in it, as we have seen that a small meal is better for a person if there is love there, for love will sweeten even a meal of vegetables, and hatred will bitter the food of a manger bull, and external happiness and apparent pleasure are not fruitless, only internal rest and love and confidence in Hashem, for in Him will be refined and enriched his soul:
text.14_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: A man of anger will provoke a judge, there is a difference between a quarrel and a judge, the judge is the one who is discussing something and the thing being discussed is the cause of the quarrel, and a quarrel includes any quarrel that may occur, and he said that a man of anger is a quarreler, someone who is in his nature to argue claims and find legal solutions, is a quarreler, and a man of anger will provoke a judge, and he said below(29:21) A man of anger will provoke a judge and a man of anger is a great sinner, and we explain the difference between anger and wrath, that anger is the fuel of internal anger and wrath is external anger, and it is also clear that a man of anger by wanting to harm his friend will provoke a judge, and he finds some plot to seek justice, and a man of anger whose anger burns even more intensely in his heart is a great sinner, and he harms his friend without justice and discussion, only with murder and slander, and here he said that sometimes A man who is angry will provoke a judge, and he will seek to exhaust his anger through the judge and through the judicial process, and from the judge will he not provoke a quarrel, although when the other party is long-tempered, and gives him a soft answer, and a soft answer will return anger, then the quarrel will be quieted, because he will appease him with soft words, and even if the judge comes in anger, the anger will subside and the quarrel will subside:
text.14_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: A lazy person's path is like a hedge and a straight path is paved There is a difference between a path and a path, that the path is the great path that goes from city to city, and the path is the path that goes from city to villages, and he said that the lazy person will be lazy to walk, and also the great path that many walk on will seem to him as if he had to walk on a hedge, which is difficult to cross because it is a hedge and a fence and thatch, and because the hedge is a hedge that pierces the feet of the passerby, and the upright also the irregular path to many is paved, as if it were a straight and easy path to cross, and what the lazy person compared to the upright is from the side of the one who is compared to being lazy, who is lazy to walk the path of wisdom, whose fixed path also seems to him as if it were full of thorns, who thinks that it is impossible for him to conquer his desires and go against his instincts, and when he does not go In its individual ways, but the righteous whose fence is straight is his heart straight and inclined to goodness, also the private host who walks in it on the path of piety and righteousness is paved, because the desires and passions of another's heart will not fight with him, as is the difference between a righteous person and a righteous one:
text.14_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise son makes his father happy, it has already been said above (10:1) A wise son makes his father happy, and a foolish son makes his mother happy, and there he speaks of what will happen of itself, that through wisdom the father will be happy, and through folly the mother will be happy, and here he speaks of the time when the son will grow up, when then the wise son, who inherits the laws of wisdom and walks in them, will strive to make his father happy with the good of his deeds, which is also the laws of wisdom to make his children happy, and the fool who is drawn after his desires, actually despises his mother, which is also one of the follies to despise her for correcting him in his ways:
text.14_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: A feast of joy for the heartless. The heartless is one who has no governing power at all to stop him from walking on a known path, as the saying goes, "And also on the path that the fool walks, his heart is lacking," etc., and he said, "In the lips of the wise you will find wisdom and a tribe to the heartless body, because he is like an animal that has no power of a leader within and needs a force from without to lead him on the path, which is the tribe, and he has turned from the wise in whose lips you will find wisdom and it will lead him, and when the heartless finds a feast and a tribe he will rejoice in it, because even the wicked are ultimately heartless, as the saying goes, "And the wicked will die in the lack of heart." Indeed, the man has wisdom, already knows the straight path according to understanding (since uprightness is in understanding as above) and he is right to walk, a guide and signs on the path that are signs of wisdom, because of himself he will walk uprightly from the side of his understanding, and will not err:
text.14_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: Break thoughts without a secret, I have already explained that there is a difference between a thought, a piece of advice, and a stratagem. All possible aspects that may arise in a person's mind in his thoughts are called thoughts. If one takes advice and chooses one piece of advice to do, this is called advice, and if one takes advice and combines many pieces of advice one after the other, so that if he does not achieve what he wants with one piece of advice, he will do another, this is called a stratagem. And the thoughts that arise in his mind must be kept secret because if he reveals them, they will be broken by enemies or those who seek his harm, and the advice that he comes up with from those thoughts will not succeed. Then there is a need for many pieces of advice, so that if one piece of advice is broken, another will be done, as the saying goes: "A war will be waged against you by stratagems." And for this, there is a need for a multitude of advisers, so that even if the advice of one adviser is broken, one piece of advice from the many will prevail:
text.14_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: A man is happy when he answers his mouth and speaks at the right time. What is good? He who has the laws of wisdom prepared on his lips until he is asked about something, will be able to answer immediately. There is more happiness than this, and it is known that language hints at wisdom. And if he answers a word at the right time at the right time to the matter, then he is good, because he will be useful with his wisdom at the right time, and this is the purpose of goodness to be useful at the right time, and this is more than the previous one, which is happy for him alone, because in this he will also benefit others at the right time:
text.14_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: I will live a life above the wise in order to turn away from the grave below. The wise will note to himself that the path of life is up and the path of death is down, and although it is difficult to go up and very easy to go down, since the force of gravity inherent in bodies will assist and bring him down, but the ascent up is against the force of gravity, 27. When he knows that if he goes down, he will certainly strive with all his might to go up and not down. Likewise, the wise will understand with his intellect that he is above the path of life, R.L. that if he goes up, he will follow the path of the soul and the path of the intellect that are rooted above, there he will attain eternal life, and he will strive to ascend the ladder of intellect so that he will turn away from rebellion to the path of the body and its desires that are rooted below, where is the grave and eternal destruction:
text.14_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: The house of the proud will the Lord tear down and establish the boundary of the widow, when you see a house of the proud built on the boundary of the widow, which is her weakness, and there is no one to fight a quarrel, and the proud will build a house on its boundary, know that there is a watcher who will fight a quarrel, and will tear down the house and uproot it to establish the boundary of the widow on its own place, for the Lord executes justice for the oppressed, the orphan, and the widow, and the way of the wicked will be turned aside, and this is a corner in the faith of providence where there is no hand of nature and no power to rule:
text.14_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: The Lord detests evil thoughts and pure words of kindness, the Lord detests one who speaks pure words of kindness and evil thoughts, whose mouth speaks kindness and pure words, and within himself he lays his ambush and his thoughts are evil:
text.14_Chapter, 26_Verse, 0_Comment: <b>A person who is greedy and gains wealth dishonestly, do not think that this greed will increase the honor of his house. On the contrary, this is a person who is greedy, as it is said: "Woe to him who is greedy, evil to his house, etc., for a stone from a wall will cry out, etc. On the contrary, someone who hates even gifts and does not enjoy the wealth of others, only what he gains by his own efforts, do not say that he will die of hunger or fall ill from overwork. On the contrary, he will live, because everything depends on Hashem's providence:
text.14_Chapter, 27_Verse, 0_Comment: The heart of a righteous man will ponder to answer, the laws of justice are that he will not let his mouth speak until he has considered the matter with his mind, and not only what he is saying, but also what needs to be answered and answered. The heart of a righteous man will ponder and consider what to answer, and whether he answers or not, as the saying goes, "And know what to answer the heretic, do not answer a fool like his master," and it is commanded not to say anything that is not heard, and the like, in a matter that he will not answer until he has considered in his heart. However, the wicked do not utter words that are not in the heart, only the mouth of the wicked utters evil things, because evil words are evil to the ear, and gossip and flattering words, originate in their mouths, not in their hearts:
text.14_Chapter, 28_Verse, 0_Comment: The Lord is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous, providence continues after a person's actions, whoever distances himself from the Lord is far from Him, and whoever draws near to Him is near to Him, until the Lord is near to the righteous and hears their prayer, as the Lord is near to all who call upon Him, and you will not ask why He acts and changes according to prayer, because in what a person draws near to Him, He is close to Him and there is no change in it, and the wicked themselves distance themselves from the Lord:
text.14_Chapter, 29_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 15:30): The light of the eyes... (Proverbs 15:30): A listening ear... - Says:
text.14_Chapter, 29_Verse, 1_Comment: If a person sees something good in his eyes, this light will rejoice the heart, which is where the spiritual powers reside; and good news heard from afar will only nourish the bones, which are the building blocks of the body and physical powers. And the joy of the heart is greater than the nourishment of the bones, and spiritual and higher than it, since the heart - from it comes the results of life for the whole body. Therefore:
text.14_Chapter, 29_Verse, 2_Comment: An ear that hears the rebuke of life. Do not be satisfied with hearing good things from afar. Only stay among the wise, to see the wise themselves and see their deeds. And (?): The use of Torah is greater than its study, for the sight of the eye is more effective than the hearing of the ear, for the light of the eyes will gladden the heart.
text.14_Chapter, 31_Verse, 0_Comment: A person who breaks a moral code is distressed by his soul, and hearing a rebuke buys a heart. The difference between morals and rebuke has already been explained. Morals frighten with fear of punishment, which is primarily a mental punishment for the hereafter, and one who breaks a moral code does not feel about his soul and its destruction, and thus his soul is distressed, and rebuke is the argument from the mind. Now, the heartless is one who does not have the power to govern at all, and is like an animal that does without a heart, only according to the pull of the body and its desires. And this person will not buy a heart through fear of morals, because he does not know at all what is good and what is bad, only through the pain itself, as the saying goes: And a tribe is a heartless body, like an animal that is drawn by a tribe, but if he hears rebuke, then he will understand in his heart and buy a heart that he lacked until now, like one who buys something from the hand of a seller:
text.14_Chapter, 32_Verse, 0_Comment: Fear of Hashem is a moral lesson, the interpreter of his words, wisdom needs morals, as in the saying, "To know wisdom and morals, because since wisdom has two paths, the path of wisdom and the path of folly, and the inclination of the heart always draws the path of folly, it is necessary to chastise the powers of the soul, which will rule over the creatures of the heart and submit them to wisdom, and this is called morals. And what is morals? Fear of Hashem, which depicts that a great king stands over him and sees his actions and demands an account from him, and this chastises the powers of the soul, and the one who violates this morals chastises his divine soul, which is connected to Hashem, who always watches over his actions. And he who hears reproof, he has inclined his ear to reproof according to the reason that shows him that the path of wisdom is good from his own point of view, and this is honorable, as it is said, "And he who keeps reproof will be honored," because he does not act out of fear, but out of his own understanding. And this will be through humility, because the proud will not hear reproof and will harden his heart to respond to the reproof of wisdom. Therefore, he said that before honor is humility:
text.15_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: A person has a heart of hearts, the heart arranges and arranges what he will speak. And as for the choice in the hand of man, he evaluates many systems and different ways of what to answer, and in 27 the final and the answer of the tongue is what, and he needs help from above to give a good answer, R"l the final action, and in particular the word of the tongue is what, as it says, And I prayed to the Hashem of heaven and said to the king who prayed for the answer of the tongue to come to him properly:
text.15_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes and the content of the Spirits of Hashem, the ways of the soul are very many, and it is not for a man to choose the pure path without a trace, only Hashem, who is the content and measures the spirit that raises the images on the heart, R. L. Sometimes a man will walk the path of righteousness and mercy and he comes by the image of the proud, who does righteousness in order to be proud, walks the path of humility and lowliness of spirit, and is rooted in his spirit by pride, who wants to be said to be humble, and so on. Similarly, there is a leveling of the spirit, that the king and the high priest whose spirit is high and lofty must walk a more excellent path and lift up his heart in the ways of Hashem, and 27. Man did not know only Hashem alone, he was limited 27 according to the laws of wisdom:
text.15_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 16:3): Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts will be established - Since thoughts are many and flow across the soul, and they have no foundation or foundation, if a person does all of his actions only for the Lord, to magnify the glory of the Lord and to do His will, until the Lord is the purpose of his actions, then his thoughts have a foundation and foundation, so that he will not only think about doing what is the glory of the Lord and His will.
text.15_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 16:4): All the Lord's actions are for His benefit - explains in what way his actions will be attributed to the Lord, because the Lord has acted for His benefit, and all creation - He created for His glory, and He wants all of man's actions to be directed toward His glory and for His name to be sanctified in His creations.
text.15_Chapter, 3_Verse, 1_Comment: And even if you see the wicked one, who defiles the honor of Hashem and does against His will, and he succeeds and exists, this too is for the glory of Hashem, because he is prepared for the day of evil, for there is a day appointed for him to receive his punishment, and then his name will be sanctified, as it is said: When He executes judgment on the wicked, his name is magnified in the world.
text.15_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: The Lord's abomination is every haughty heart, meaning that although the Lord does not punish evil thoughts and actions, all of which have not borne fruit for a person's actions, and likewise, He will not punish the actions immediately through special supervision, He will only hide His face from the sinner and leave him until the time comes. Not so is the haughty heart, who thinks in his heart that he is in a very high position and therefore breaks out with all the strength of his soul to think that his heart is a dog of Hashem, and therefore does not listen to the words of the Torah and the teachers, and transgresses the boundaries of morality. This is a root that bears fruit and a wormwood and is an abomination to the Lord until He punishes us hand to hand, R. L. not by means, and will not be cleansed from punishment, because the punishment that comes by nature is sometimes a wicked person prolongs his evil because he hopes that he will repent. Not so is the haughty heart, where there is no hope that he will improve his way:
text.15_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: By kindness and truth, an iniquity will be atoned for, although even one who wronged with malice, Hashem has provided that he should hold fast to kindness and truth to perform acts of kindness between a person and his neighbor without payment of a reward, which is kindness of truth, and also to hold fast to the measure of truth with care, as the wise man says (Blessings of the Lord). Kindness is G-d and truth is Torah, and in this iniquity will be atoned for, as the saying goes: If the iniquity of the house of Eli is atoned for with a sacrifice and an offering, with a sacrifice and an offering, it is not atoned for, but it is atoned for in the Torah and by performing acts of kindness, 27. Better is he who walks in the fear of the Lord, who through fear will turn away from evil, and will not need atonement at all, as the saying goes: Blessed is the one who marries a transgressor, blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute iniquity:
text.15_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: In the will of Hashem, the ways of a man, he has already said that his will is pure, that to achieve Hashem's will, he must be pure, meaning that he must not pursue an external appearance in his spirit, and he must always stand in innocence, and then Hashem will reconcile his enemies with him, who are his internal enemies, who are images of desires, who will be at peace with him after no evil image arises in his heart, which is the boundary of innocence, and by having his internal enemies reconciled, Hashem will also reconcile his external enemies with him, measure for measure, just as He reconciled with Hashem the enemies of the divine soul, which is an allusion in the Mishnah, that the enemies of Hashem will reconcile with Hashem, and they are the images of desire, and so will Hashem reconcile the enemies of the body with him:
text.15_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: A little in righteousness is better than much fruit without justice, it is itself the verse in Psalms 37: Better a little for the righteous than a multitude of many wicked people. Which explains the reason that the arms of the wicked will be broken and the Lord upholds the righteous, that the little of the righteous is upheld by the Lord, and the much of the wicked is under the providence of the Lord to destroy him, and so it is with his wealth and possessions, the little he has obtained through righteousness is under the providence of the Lord and will provide sustenance, and the much fruit he has obtained without justice, the Lord will destroy him, and in this there is no duplication with the verse above: A little is better in the fear of the Lord, which there speaks of pleasure itself, that what he gathers in the fear of the Lord, he will find in it pleasure and rest, and even though the days of the poor are evil, in all this this little is better for him, than the great treasure of the good heart, a feast always in which he will find turmoil and there is no peace for the wicked:
text.15_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's heart will consider his way, and the Lord will prepare his steps. The root of the word "thought" when it comes to action indicates thoughts that depart from the ordinary or inappropriate thoughts. Jeremiah already said (10) I know that it is not in man's own way, not in man who walks and prepares his steps. The way is what he chooses which way to walk, and the step is what he steps with his feet. And although the choice was given to man, 27 the organs of movement in which his action will be completed, the Lord moves them with His power, between the tongue that brings out the thought in matters of speech, as it says to a man from the dispositions of the heart, and what is the tongue that answers between the feet that complete his thought in matters of movement on the path he has chosen, and since it is not in man who walks and prepares his steps, because the organs of movement are in the hand of the Lord, so it is not in man's way, because the mover can hinder his movement if the Lord does not desire his way, and He said (Psalms 37) Why are the steps of a man prepared and his way? He will desire that he fall, but he will not be cast down, etc., because even the steps of a mighty man are from Hashem, and Hashem desires his way, although the choice of the path is from man, Hashem hinders his movement if he does not desire this way, and when you see the righteous man fall because his feet will not stand on the path he has chosen, know that he will not be cast down because Hashem supports his hand, and He hinders his movement so that he may rise and walk on the path that is good in the sight of Hashem. And he said to the man, "What is the steps of a man and a man? How can he understand his way? And if you see a man's step he considers, R'al who thinks unworthy advice about his way, know that it will not be beneficial, because Hashem will prepare his step, and he will not be able to walk without the will of Hashem:
text.15_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: A king's lips are like a charm, and in a lawsuit he will not conceal his mouth. The lips are the external speech and the mouth is the internal speech in wisdom. And behold, everything the king utters with his lips, even if it is for a case, is like a charm that they will rush to guess and decide from, because the way he utters with his lips and the quality of his external speech with which he dresses the words of his mouth is like a charm to decide on great matters. Therefore, in a lawsuit, he will not cover his mouth with a coat. Every word of his mouth that he speaks with wisdom to decide the lawsuit, he will speak clearly so that there will be no room for error, lest then his mouth fall into the hands of fraud and open betrayal.
text.15_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: The scales and balances of justice are the work of the Lord, all the stones of the pocket. A scale is greater than a scale and is actually used to measure the circle, which is the circular path used to measure a place that is close to the area of ​​the object. In the scales, an object to be weighed is placed in one pan and weighted stones in the other pan to see if they are directed against each other. He said that the Lord has a scale to weigh a person's ways, his customs, and his circles and direct them toward righteousness, and He also has scales of justice to weigh the deeds of people and to reward them, good or bad, according to their measures. And what are the stones of the pocket that He places inside the scales? They are His work, R.L. Hashem arranged all the work He did, to weigh the works of the first of the chosen ones with them, that just as a person would do and place his works on the scale, so will the works of Hashem and the ways of nature and the battle be directed against it, as it says, "If you will listen attentively to My commandments, I will give rain to your land in its season, lest your heart be deceived and stop the heavens." In the works of Hashem there are all kinds of weighing stones, large and small, all of which are stones of justice, directed in the scale of the works of Hashem in the great world, against the other scale in which the person who chooses will place his works on the scale of choice in his small world, and the two scales will always weigh together, both for good and for evil:
text.15_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: The abomination of kings, as I have already explained (Isaiah 9) that the establishment of the kingdom is based on judgment between man and his neighbor, but the establishment of the throne and its preparation is based on righteousness, as it says, "Prepare it in judgment from now on and feast it in righteousness forever" (Isaiah 9). And since only through righteousness, which is the law, will a throne be established that it will have existence, then doing evil that he has turned righteousness into an abomination of kings, for this will destroy the establishment of their throne and their kingdom:
text.15_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: The will of kings is the tongue of justice. Justice is in the matter of judgment, that judgment be according to justice, not a crooked judgment, as the saying goes, and judge the poor with justice. And this is the will of kings, because a king will reign for justice, and the righteous are a step above justice, and he is the one who does what is right, above the law, and also includes the righteousness of opinions. The king will love him, and this is more than the will:
text.15_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: The wrath of the king is the angels of death, and a wise man will atone for it. Anger lies in the heart, and its manifestation to take revenge is called anger. Here, the wrath of a layman is not dangerous because Hashem will take revenge immediately. However, when the king is aroused in his wrath, he is the angels who send death, because in his wrath he will destroy many. It is necessary to seek a wise man who, through his wisdom, knows how to atone for sin and to turn away his wrath. It has a saying about the wrath of the supreme king, which aroused the angels of death, and a wise man will atone for it, like Phinehas turned away his wrath, etc., and atoned for the children of Israel, and said, "We would have destroyed them if it had not been for Moses, his chosen one," etc., to turn away his wrath from the destroyer:
text.15_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: In the light of the face of the king of life, he is turned upward, and after a wise man has turned away from the heat, the angels of death depart, and then in the light of the light of the face of the king, which is a sign that the heat has departed, he will find life, which he has turned away from death, and if he continues to produce his will, he will be like a cloud from the sky. And behold, Lakman (19:12) growled like a kuffar, a king's wrath and dew on the grass of his desire. The wrath is less than the heat, because it is an internal sadness that is expressed over something, and it is not in the heat only when abundance and desire prevent it, and then a person should not approach him, just as one should not approach the kuffar when he is growling, and in 27 he does not send death outside his boundary because the kuffar does not go out on his prey outside his dwelling, (which is the act of the lion, not the kuffar) only in his dwelling no living thing should approach him, and then after his will has returned, he will return to bestow and bestow his goodness, and all are satisfied like the dew that comes constantly on the grass to moisten it. But the wrath of a king will send angels of death outside his boundary, and it takes a wise man to atone, and if his will returns after it has been withheld for many days, and the grass was thirsty for the rain of his goodness, his will is like a thick cloud of dew, as if the rain had been withheld for many days, and it returned to satisfy the withered and tossed grass. Without water, and also when He wills, He will return to bestow His goodness and blessing upon them after they have stopped and prevented them from reviving and showering goodness and grace:
text.15_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: Buy wisdom, what is better than a hoe, and buy understanding is chosen than money. Wisdom is the accepted teachings on how to behave in all the qualities of the soul and the standards, and understanding is that which understands a thing from a thing of itself, both in matters of wisdom that produces a saying, and in matters about which the mind judges according to the intellectual inferences between truth and falsehood, and there is a difference between money and the hoe, which is the treasury of nature and the hoe, which will be used to spend and trade other things with. Gold will be appropriated in treasures and will not be taken out, as the saying goes, for the trade of money is better than the trade of money, and the hoe is its harvest. Now wisdom is a virtue, he will gather it in the treasures of his heart and will not take it out to trade with it, it is only the grain that one eats to the satisfaction of the soul, and alas Buy wisdom, what is better than the hoe, which is a more valuable possession than the hoe, because it is good in itself from its own side. But understanding is traded in which, by means of inferences, one produces a saying and understands and exchanges an idea In the idea of ​​rationality, rationality and profit are likened to something that is traded, and on this the intellect likens it to the imagination of money, which is not good in itself, but only in its price, for which other goods are received in exchange, but the buyers of the intellect choose money, because in exchange they will take rational, valuable things:
text.15_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: The path of the upright is one who turns away from evil. The upright is one whose nature inclines toward righteousness and who does not have an internal war in his spirit like the righteous. And this one has a paved and established path, where no obstacle is found, and he does not stubbornly follow his path. In this he turns away from evil, because his path is paved with desires and the desires of the heart, as the saying goes, "And the path of the upright is paved." But he who does not have a paved path and must walk on an unpaved path is dangerous, because many fight against him to divert him from his path and to kill him with the death of the soul. And he who guards his soul, created through his path, with excessive guarding, may not fall into one of the pitfalls and may not incline to crooked ways and become prey to the desires of the heart and to the evil thoughts and snares of the soul:
text.15_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: (18-19) Before the fall of a genius, etc., it is good to be humble, etc., humility and pride are both in choice, the proud elevates a person above his level, and the humble humiliates to the point of knowing and recognizing the value of man because he has no room for pride because he is flesh and blood, and humility is the last extreme against humility, which is the middle between pride and humiliation, the humble only feels his dignity when he is humble because of his choice, and the humble, the images of his spirit will humiliate him until he does not feel at all when they humiliate him, and in all measures the path that is offered is good, but in pride, be very, very warned, O humble, it is good to go to the last extreme, but it is not good to have a natural, imperceptible low spirit, only it is good for the humble, that there be humiliation because of humility, which is a choice of the intellect according to wisdom and righteousness, and the haughty is one whose images of the spirit are raised to the heart and are exalted to be proud, and 27 have not yet come into effect, because the heart governs On the images of the spirit and can humble with his spirit, but if they act on the heart until he is amazed by them and becomes proud of heart, then he becomes abhorrent (as in, "Every proud heart is an abomination to Hashem, and he will receive punishment, as in, "Hand to hand will not cleanse"), then he will lament in his heart the measure of pride, and be called proud, and if it is added to that that he is also rich and
