powerful, then there is a proud and arrogant person in his heart and he is close to Hashem who will break him, as in, "Before a break a man's heart is lifted up," and here he said, "Before a break a proud man," and he who is only proud, and has not yet lifted his heart and has not come to the point of pride, is close to failure, after the proud man has fought with him and easily falls, and this is "Before the failure of a proud man," and when he falls, after the obstacle is the breaking, then the arrogant man will be promoted, as in, "Before the break of a proud man," because the pride of his spirit rules over the heart until he comes to the point of pride, and therefore it is good for him to be humble of spirit. The humble, to be lowly in spirit to the point of humiliation, so that he will not stumble and so that he will not break, divides the spoils of the proud, even though it may seem to him that he is dividing the spoils and great prosperity with them, because suddenly he will break and be humbled, but the end of humility is honor, as the saying goes: And before honor is humility:
text.15_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: He who is knowledgeable about a matter will find good, R. L. He who does his business without knowledge and does not pay attention to choosing the means that lead to a desired end will not find good, which is the end he did not seek. But he who is knowledgeable about a matter and seeks with his mind how and in what manner to do it, will find good, and there is a difference between successful and knowledgeable. Success is by chance according to luck, and the knowledgeable will think with his mind to find the good means, and then he will find good as someone who searched and found what he sought. Indeed, there is another way that is not knowledgeable about his words at all, who only trusts in Hashem and believes that Hashem will do everything according to providence, then he is happy, because this is the happiness and providential spiritual success, that the happy is greater than the successful, which is the happiness of the soul:
text.15_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise man is called wise. We have already explained the difference between a wise man and a wise man of heart. The wise man has received the laws of wisdom, and in all this there is still a war in his heart against the images of lust and malice. However, the wise man of heart is one whose heart, which is his governing force, has been imprinted in nature on the images of wisdom and has no internal war at all, because through habit and study this becomes natural to him. Here the wise man understands one thing from another, and he is busy understanding the laws of wisdom until finally they return to him as knowledge, so that he knows clear knowledge as if it were tangible. The wise man will also easily conquer the images of lust after he understands the laws of wisdom, as in (14:32) wisdom will rest in the heart of a wise man, but in 27:13 much work is required until he understands everything, as in (15:14) a wise heart will seek knowledge, and he said here that the wise man of heart whose images of wisdom have returned to him as nature will be called A wise man, who, although he did not attain the flavors of wisdom through the ways of reason, understood them from the nature of wisdom itself, which does not contradict the nature of his soul and its properties. And now the wise man will copy wisdom into a general knowledge that is implied by the lips (as in, "On the lips of a wise man you will find wisdom") and he said that even the wise man, who has reached the level of a wise man from his nature and habit, through the sweetness of the lips will add a lesson. If he copies wisdom into his lips as something known in the knowledge, which is accustomed to the external lips, he will add a lesson, he will continue to take new ones in the general knowledge of wisdom, as in, "A wise man will hear and add a lesson," because he does not understand according to the invention of the mind and its ways, only according to the habit of wisdom, which is taken in the Kabbalah. Therefore, he said the language of the lesson, which is the Kabbalah:
text.15_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: A source of life whose owner is all Now, let us explain how the wise heart will understand the laws of wisdom until it reaches the totality of knowledge. Explain this source of life from which the wise heart draws knowledge. The owner of the source is the intellect, which although it will not attain the laws of wisdom by the power of the intellect, will attain them by the power of the intellect, which is a unique power that a person has to understand invisible truths, and to understand also the laws of wisdom and spiritual matters that are sublime from human understanding. There is also a good intellect, which is the Holy Spirit, which will be applied to the wise heart, and as stated above (14:15) The law of a wise heart is a source of life. A good intellect will give grace, which I explained is also a source of life and it will give grace and pardon from Hashem to understand the sublime, and it will clarify The morals of the wicked, because although wisdom and morals of the wicked are in this, because they are content and impose philosophical limitations on the laws of wisdom and on the roots of morality Those who are built on the fear of Hashem, the intellect will discern truth according to the morals of the intellect, which will chastise the wicked and discern their misfortune and their success according to the intellect, and this is in the power of the wise-hearted, as it says: "When wisdom enters your heart and knowledge delights your soul, to save you from the evil way from a man who speaks perverse things," and as it says: "And a wicked servant is a wise-hearted one, for through the wisdom of the heart he knows the morals of the wicked and the elimination of their misfortune and success."
text.15_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise heart will instruct his mouth, the interpreter of this stage is the wise one who has acquired wisdom until the person is called by the name of a wise heart, this heart will instruct his mouth, the mouth alludes to the word of wisdom, when he speaks in the laws of wisdom, the spirit of the mind that is educated in the truths of the laws of wisdom will be applied to him, and then on his lips he will add a lesson when he speaks with his lips to clarify them with the examples of knowledge that this is implied in the lips, he will add a lesson, as it says in verse 21, and sweet lips he will add a lesson:
text.15_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: The nectar of honey, the words of Amiri Noam, is sweet to the soul and healing to the body, belongs above, and on his lips Joseph took nectar of honey, because when knowledge came to his lips, then he would sweeten with knowledge the laws of wisdom until he found sweetness in them, not as something that had no taste, but he found in them the nectar of honey and the words they are pleasure, which is the spiritual sweetness that comes from spiritually sophisticated people, and he explains that the nectar of honey is not a physical sweetness to the palate, only sweet to the soul, and likewise the words of Noam are not special to the soul alone, which is abstracted from the body, but also a healing to the body, until he achieves truth in the intellect that is bound to the body, and the Spirit of Hashem will fill all his chambers with precious and pleasant wealth, and he will also restore the wretched by his teaching of the morality of reason:
text.15_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: (22-23) There is a straight path before a man, a soul of toil is his toil, he returns to the top to say to him, "The nectar of honey is pleasant words," and he explains to him that there is a straight path before a man, which at its beginning seems to be straight to fulfill the desires and wishes of the body, but its end is the ways of death, because the end of the body is to die and waste away, and then the spiritual soul will also die, and he says to him, "Is it possible that a soul of toil will toil by the necessity that its mouth imposes on it? that the mouth that wants to eat will force and compel the spiritual soul to toil always without ceasing (as in, all the labor of a man is for his mouth, and even the soul will not be satisfied)." And he explains to him this fact, that is not the essence of man the eternal soul within him, and the root of life is the eternal life that is the life of the soul, and man was created to live the spiritual life, which comes by putting to death the body and its wishes, and although it is a path full of thorns at its beginning, will it not find life? In the end, my life will last until after I return to an eternal paradise, and is there greater folly than for this precious soul to abandon its spirituality and toil through the necessity of the mouth that wants to eat and drink, eat and drink, because tomorrow we will die and nothing will remain to the soul from all its labor? This is what the educated mind will say about the life of the soul and the matters of its spirituality and its survival after death, and it has already been said above (14:9) The wicked will be punished, a heart that knows the bitterness of its soul, there is a straight path before a man, and its end is the ways of death, which I explained there that even the wicked know in their hearts that they are guilty of the soul, because their path is straight in their eyes to choose a life of vanity, the end of which is the death of the spiritual soul, and their heart knows the bitterness of their soul and sorrow for this, and therefore he also said here that in these words the wise heart will chasten the wicked with honeyed nectar, pleasant words, and will turn them from the path of their error:
text.15_Chapter, 26_Verse, 0_Comment: A wicked man digs evil, after he has thought through the path of wisdom that clothes him with humility, confidence, and humility, and has returned those who have gone astray to the path by the grace of his lips, he thinks through the foolishness that he has become. There is a wicked man, who completely breaks the yoke of heaven from above him, and he is a wicked man who digs a pit in the depths and in secret for his friend to fall, and on his lips burns as a scorching fire, for he speaks with the enthusiasm of the flames of love until the scorching of the burnt one is visible on the lips, as the saying goes, slag silver is plated on clay. Burning lips and an evil heart, his lips will speak love, and within him he will lay his ambush:
text.15_Chapter, 27_Verse, 0_Comment: A man of perversities will send a judge, and there is a man of perversities who perverts the truth and the ways of wisdom, and his way of sending a judge is as follows: (above 6) Perversities in his heart are a bad grove of judges, and there is a scolder who is always complaining, saying that his friend hates him and cheers him on, as in "We have quarreled in your tents and said, 'The Lord hates us,'" and as in "The words of a scolder are like those who quarrel, and he is the one who keeps the judges, as in "When he is not angry, he will keep silent in a judge (26), and he also separates the one who loves and cheers the scolder and the one who teaches and guides in a good way, saying that he seeks his own evil:
text.15_Chapter, 28_Verse, 0_Comment: A man of anger will tempt his neighbor, and there is one who harms his neighbor by tempting him to lead him down an unwholesome path, and all of these are harmful and corrupting:
text.15_Chapter, 29_Verse, 0_Comment: He closes his eyes to think of perversions, in what he hints at with his eyes through advice, he already thinks of perversions, as the saying goes, "He winks with his eyes, perversions in his heart." And when he winks his lips and speaks through a hint, then all evil is already done, as if with a hint of the eye he begins, and with a tongue and a wink of the lips all his evil ends, so the evil deed becomes easy in his eyes:
text.15_Chapter, 30_Verse, 0_Comment: The crown of glory of old age, the return is the crown of glory that we are obligated to give to the elderly for having lived long and done much good and fulfilled their purpose, but this crown will not be found only in the path of righteousness, for then everyone who has added days has added mitzvot and maht, but the wicked have continued to do evil and will not wear the crown of days. And also Yal"p Ad 44 45 The fear of the Lord will add days, and it will not be good for the wicked and he will not prolong his days, and after considering the deeds of wicked people, about whom he already said above (ibid.) A man without a will, etc. Therefore, suddenly will Ido come, he also said here that in the path of this wicked one will not find a crown of old age, because suddenly he will break and there is no cure:
text.15_Chapter, 31_Verse, 0_Comment: A long-suffering man is better than a warrior. The warrior who does not lose his temper and take revenge on his enemies shows his heroism in overcoming his external enemy. However, if he listens to the laws of wisdom so as not to take revenge and overcomes the urges of jealousy and revenge that would command his organs to take action to take revenge, he is better than a warrior, because he has overcome his more difficult internal enemy. And there are those who lose their temper and are short-tempered (ibid. 14:17) who, although they do not take action to take revenge, 27 the spirit raises images of revenge on the heart and harbors enmity, as the saying goes, "And a short-tempered man brings forth a plague." But he who is thus governed by his spirit, to subdue his enemies so that images of revenge do not rise at all on the heart, is better than a city besieger, because the spirit is like a fortress city filled with a great force of the old and foolish instincts, which are images of the spirit for all evil purposes. And if he overcomes the spirit, he has conquered the entire small city, and that is heroism. More than a city conqueror, he crosses with might and power:
text.15_Chapter, 32_Verse, 0_Comment: In the lap of fate is cast and all its judgment is from Hashem. There are things that seem to be subject to chance and are overseen by Hashem, and where the power of human choice and effort ceases, the eye of providence will appear, as in a matter settled between people and they cast lots to determine by fate who will receive the portion being discussed. Even though the fate was cast in the lap of the North of man and is subject to chance, the eye of Hashem's providence will nevertheless appear over it, and the judgment that fate will bring out is not chance but is from Hashem, as in the division of the land and the like, where fate was under the providence of Hashem:
text.16_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: Better is a loaf of bread and peace in it than a house full of sacrifices of strife, the apparent success is not true success, and sometimes we see a wicked man succeeding and his house full of great sacrifices, and the righteous man is content with a loaf of bread, who has no whole bread, only a loaf that is sliced, and not a butterfly to the loaf, only a loaf of bread, and in 27 the poor will be more successful than the rich, if one has peace in his house and the other has strife, whether in his house or with the people of his city, which is the obstacle to the apparent success, because the root of success is inner peace, so that he will be calm and successful in his soul and has nothing that hinders his mental peace, and this is the one who is truly successful, even though he eats a loaf of bread:
text.16_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise servant will rule over a shameful son. Do not think that wealth and position are the inheritance of ancestors, because everything depends on diligence and diligence. Even a servant, if he is wise, diligent, and diligent, will rule over a shameful, late, and lazy son. When the master's inheritance is divided, he will be like one of his sons and will share the inheritance. In the parable that the wise foreigner is superior to the shameful Israelite, and some of the sons of Sisera learned Torah in public, and the deed of Shemaiah and Avtalion with the high priest is eternal:
text.16_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (3-4) Affixed to silver etc. Evil listens etc., Silver in order to separate the dross from it requires a affixed, and the more precious gold, its dross is more stuck to it and to separate and refine it requires a furnace, which is a greater fire And Hashem is the examiner of hearts, to purify each one from the dross according to what it is, there is a heart to which the dross is not so stuck and is likened to silver, and it is the one who sins between good and evil famously on the part of lust, and this will be added to with a small fire, and there is the one who distorts with the eyes in matters between truth and falsehood that are in the understanding, and this is likened to gold, because sin and the intellect are more important than the deed, but its dross is more stuck to it and a greater furnace and fire are needed to purify and test it, and it is interpreted that the one who adds to silver is evil who listens to the language of evil, who listens to his desires which are wood The mind is good and evil, which we answered with language that is external to the tongue. For the difference between good and evil is known through the senses and the mind that the tongue hints at the mind, and whoever listens to the language of evil, which is lust for things that are famous and replaces good with evil, is evil, and the gold furnace is the one who listens to the language of being, which is in the understanding, and if he corrupts the understanding, he brings a break and a contradiction to being and being, and he is a lie, because he replaces the truth with a lie, and this requires a gold furnace to remove its dross and the mixtures of the qualities that are in it:
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 17:5): He who mocks the poor despises his maker, and he who rejoices in the Lord will not be cleansed - We have already written in the verse "He who oppresses the poor despises his maker," that the one who makes the poor and creates them certainly has prepared his livelihood for them, and the oppressor despises his maker, who created them in vain. And here he added, that even the "who mocks the poor because he is weak in strength, and has no means of livelihood, despises his maker, who certainly has a good purpose in him, and nothing of his creations is left to chance.
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 1_Comment: And some came in the way of mockery, and some came in the way of revenge because they hated him, saying:
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 2_Comment: * Whoever comes in the way of mockery - despite doing it,
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 3_Comment: * And he who "rejoices over an enemy in the way of revenge, will not be cleansed from punishment, as it is said (Proverbs 24:17): "Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, etc."
text.16_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: The crown of old men is sons and daughters. Man exists in man from the standpoint of his soul, and exists in the species from the standpoint of his body, and since he exists in the species, the old men are adorned with sons and daughters, so that although old age is the testimony that he is about to pass away from the world, his sons and daughters will remain in his place, and the sons will boast in the merit of their fathers, for in this they exist in man and their righteousness stands for their sons after them:
text.16_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: It is not fitting for a villain to speak excessively, the villain is the opposite of the generous, and although the villain is the extreme opposite to generosity, and there is no way to promise giving and kindness, 27 if he promises something, not only is it not fitting for him to speak a lie and he must keep his promise, because he must also be careful to do everything he promised without fail, and if he speaks excessively, that is, more than he gives, it is a disgrace to him, because although the villain does not volunteer, 27 his promise will not be broken even if the generous person speaks falsely, which is a disgrace from three sides, whether on the part of the person who is generous, or on the part of the promise, not only that he did not keep the promise as promised, he did not keep the promise at all and is a lie:
text.16_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: A gem, came to teach a warning about accepting a bribe, because a bribe will arouse the eyes of the wise, even if he thinks that he will not sway the judgment and judge truly according to the laws of wisdom, a bribe will arouse the eyes of reason and make it seem to him that the truth is true and that he does not distort justice. He said that a bribe is like a gem in the eyes of its owner. There is a stone that has the ability to bring favor to the bearer, and the one who carries the stone seems to himself that he does not need to make any effort because whoever he turns to will be wise, because he will find favor everywhere and in the eyes of everyone, even if he is not worthy. Likewise, the one who gives a bribe will not bother at all to arrange his arguments so that he will win the trial, because he trusts himself in the ability of the stone that carries it to bring favor in the eyes of the judge to do his will, and a bribe will arouse the eyes of the wise, just as a gem arouses the eyes of people without looking at the deserving, because it brings favor in its own eyes:
text.16_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: A crime that seeks love, already said that all crimes will be covered by love, here Hashem said the opposite that a crime that seeks love is covered, because it also causes love on the part of the other person, but the different thing is like a man of shame who said to Abner, "Why did you go to my father's concubines?" He separated his master and his acquaintance, and rebelled against him and became his enemy. And again, the king who seeks love covers one crime, but if he is different and commits this crime a second time, then he separates his master, because then he will no longer be forgiven, and Hashem also implies that if a person is different in sin, he will not find forgiveness, and if he sins again, he will be treated as if he had been permitted:
text.16_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (10-11) Under rebuke from the wise, etc., But rebellious, etc., the fool will not benefit from a beating because he knows the laws of wisdom, but he is deviant from them because his desire has overcome him, and beating will not benefit only the heartless, as the proverb says, "And a whip is like a whip for a heartless body, which is not rebellious and rebels with self-loathing, only its heart is lacking, and it is like an animal that is beaten with a whip to divert its path, but for the wise, a whip is more beneficial to the wise than a hundred strokes, because the fool is But rebellious, who is only rebellious with malice and through rebellion and rebellion will seek evil, because desire will force him to defy the mouth of wisdom with malice, and he will seek evil even if a cruel angel were sent to him, and no beating will benefit him, because if he were not rebellious with malice, rebuke would be enough for him, because he Truly understands only seeks evil through rebellion and rebellion:
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: "Meet a bereaved bear in a man, and a fool in his folly - The fool who meets a man with his folly is more dangerous than a bereaved bear:
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 1_Comment: * The bear is dangerous to the body, and the fool is dangerous to the soul;
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 2_Comment: * The bear rips open his heart to get the blood out, and he rips open his heart to put in foolishness and incompetence;
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 3_Comment: * The bear will sometimes defeat the man on his side, but the fool will not be defeated by his folly;
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 4_Comment: * The bear will sometimes put a man to rest, but the fool will never put his folly to rest.
text.16_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: He who repays evil for good, Hashem will repay him in kind, and although the wicked man can turn from his way, he who repays evil for good Hashem will give him in kind, and even if he returns and does good, Hashem will repay him evil for good, and evil will not depart from his house even when his deeds are good:
text.16_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: (14-15) He who releases water, etc., Justifies evil, etc., the judge who is looking for some pretext to judge and judge, is similar to someone who releases water and opens it, who first releases the pipe can delay the flow of water, but later cannot delay it, and likewise, the beginning of a judge is similar to wanting to release and open the blocked water, and the advice is that before it has arisen the judge should remove the dispute, to make a compromise between them and reconcile them, and as the Sages said, before you hear their words or when you hear their words and you do not know where the law is headed, you can tell them, "Come out and carry it out," and then the judge can tell them, "Come out and carry it out." The beginning of a judge is before the law has begun, when he has ruled on the arguments of the judge, which means when their words are heard and you do not know where the law is headed, and likewise, the dispute is abandoned before it has arisen, that is, while the dispute has not begun. And the arguments in general, but if you have heard the arguments and know the verdict of who is righteous in the judgment and who is wicked and you want to make a compromise, then you are justifying a wicked person and also condemning a righteous person by the compromise, so that the wicked person takes the little that he does not deserve, and the righteous person loses a little of what he deserves, both of which are also an abomination to Hashem:
text.16_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: Why is it a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom and a heart that is not? There is a difference between one who takes money and one who takes a price, for the one who takes money gives something that is given at a cost, but one who takes a price and in exchange, exchanges and gives in exchange for a desired thing something that he desires, and the fool, who has defined himself as a lover of lust and when he comes to buy wisdom, it seems to him that he is paying a price for wisdom, because if he holds onto the object of wisdom, he will have to give in exchange for it an object of lust, which is also something precious in his eyes, and he does not have a heart that is the power to control his desires and walk in the laws of wisdom:
text.16_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: (17-18) At all times he loves evil, etc., A heartless man strikes a blow. Here is the fence of the evil one, that he should always love his neighbor at all times, and when tribulation occurs, his love will grow even more until he becomes like a brother, willing to give his life for his neighbor as if he were his brother. Nevertheless, although the one who shouts is obligated to do everything for his neighbor, he is not obligated to collect sureties and strike a blow on his behalf, and if he does so out of love, he is a heartless man and does not see the future:
text.16_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: Loves sin loves matzah, someone who loves matzah, which is the greatest quarrel in beatings, is either by who loves sin, as in the saying, a man of great anger, who through anger even brings matzah, as in the saying, "He will only give matzah out of malice," or he loves matzah because of his pride, who thinks that he is higher than all the people, and if the one who raises his door asks for a break, a person whose house is built on a low place, only the door that is raised alone, will break the way in and out, so if he is a lowly man and opens his mouth in pride above what he is, he will break:
text.16_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: "A stubborn heart will not find good -
text.16_Chapter, 19_Verse, 1_Comment: A stubborn heart is one whose heart (which is the governing force within him) follows stubborn paths, not according to the path of wisdom, which is the right path. Even if he seeks the path of goodness according to his mind, he will not find goodness, because the path of goodness is only according to wisdom, which cannot be found by his mind, only by receiving it from the mouths of the wise. And yet, it may be that he will not do evil.
text.16_Chapter, 19_Verse, 2_Comment: But he who "turns with his tongue, whose tongue paints speech with understanding, and he whose tongue speaks perversions, which are misleading assertions and false investigations into divinity and beliefs, and goes into heresy, not only will he not find good, but he will also fall into evil, (Proverbs 23:27): For a prostitute, who is a prostitute, digs deep.
text.16_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: A fool is born to his own sorrow. The fool is sometimes endowed with great wisdom, only for his own wisdom to overpower him and blind him and lead him astray. There is a fool from birth who is born with lust by nature, and there is a fool through habit and learning, and behold, the son of a fool angers his father. And if foolishness is not natural, although he will not rejoice in him, he will not be filled with sorrow, because he hopes that he will be educated in the way of goodness and abandon foolishness. But if a fool is born from birth who is a natural fool, he is to his own sorrow, because there is no hope.
text.16_Chapter, 20_Verse, 1_Comment: And the father of a villain will not rejoice, the villain that he has become is usually generous by habit, and there are those whose villainous father teaches and educates him to be as villainous as he is and rejoices in it, but the father of a villain will not rejoice, who in the end will not rejoice in this because in the end he knows that his joy will be sorrowful:
text.16_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: A happy heart does good to the body, and a sad spirit dries up the bones, as I have already mentioned above (15:13) in the verse A happy heart does good to the face, and sadness of the heart causes a sad spirit, that there is a happy heart and a sad spirit, that the heart outwardly rejoices in the goodness of the world and success, but its inner spirit is sad and it is better for the heart to be sad and not have a sad spirit, and it is better for the heart to be sad and not to have a sad spirit, and it is said that a happy heart only does good to the body, R. L. Goya, which is the external body, as in the verse A happy heart does good to the face, but a sad spirit dries up the bones, and the essence of a person is in his interiority:
text.16_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: A bribe is a wicked person who takes to pervert the course of justice. There are several types of bribery. Some take bribes from both sides in order to benefit from their judgment, as in the saying, "The chiefs shall judge by bribery," or by a bribe taker who makes a compromise, as in the saying, "He who loves bribes and pursues bribes," or in a matter in which there is certainty that the judge will be favored over one side, but the wicked person takes bribes in order to pervert the course of justice, as in the case of the Sadducees, who said in the beginning, "Bara and Bara, let them be known," in which the general course of justice is perverted, and this bribe is taken from the bosom in secret, since the first bribe is taken openly:
text.16_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: "The face of one who understands wisdom, and the eyes of a fool are at the ends of the earth. The ways of wisdom are close to the nature of the human soul as long as it is not revealed in the lusts of this world and in the temptations of the heart's instincts that oppose the ways of wisdom. And every understanding person will see that wisdom stands before him, and is engraved on the face of his soul, which is its divine form, like mirrors that are set face to face. And when he looks at the face of his soul and its true form, he will find the form of wisdom engraved on it.
text.16_Chapter, 23_Verse, 1_Comment: Only the fool, whose soul is filled with lust, which has rusted its surface and erased the imprints of wisdom from its form, like a mirror stained with mud and slime in which no forms are discernible, seeks wisdom at the ends of the earth, as if it were something far removed from the nature of his soul, far away and opposed to its nature, and that, in his opinion, he must travel a long way with many obstacles until he finds it.
text.16_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: A foolish son is angry with his father and bitter to his mother. A foolish son, in addition to causing grief to his father, who sees him going out into bad culture, also causes him anger in that he makes his mother bitter, whose soul is bitter about his actions. In this, the father will be angry over his wife's distress, or over a quarrel he has with her. And Lakman said to his father, "He is a foolish son and a troublemaker who disturbs a woman's affairs:
text.16_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: (22-27-28) Even punishment for the righteous, etc., The darkness of his words, etc., Even a deaf wolf, etc. He said, "Here is something that is apparently not good and honest in leadership, and it is what Hashem punishes the righteous, and what strikes the generous, from which the righteous' complaint arises and is bad for him, that what punishes the righteous is not good, and what strikes the generous is against honesty, is the Lord a wrongdoer in honesty?" The Prophet answers, "Whoever knows the knowledge of the darkness of His words and does not ask this question, since he knows by knowledge that Hashem watches over and that no wrongdoing will come from Him, because He is perfect in the utmost perfection, and thus knows that the judgment of Hashem is certainly true and will not question or reveal His words from this difficulty, and whoever is a man of understanding understands the reasons for this leadership, which is to repay him for some sin he committed in this world, to benefit him in the hereafter, and similar reasons that were stated in this, and he A precious spirit, even in his inner spirit this question will not disturb him. However, even the wretched and the contented in everything, if he keeps silent and does not abandon this question, he will consider himself wise, for in this he has already acted according to the laws of wisdom, not uttering such questions with his mouth, even though he is content with his heart. And if he seals his lips completely, until even in his outward speech he does not find any doubt about this, he will be considered wise, and they will think that he has reached the stage of contemplating it with wisdom, as the saying goes:
text.17_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: For lust, one seeks separately, someone who has already separated from lust and seeks it, such as the old and the sick who have already separated from lust and who seeks and uses a trick to arouse lust, (by means of signs and the like) he will appear in all his cunning and weakness (from the word "teshut keah") because this will weaken his body in all kinds of teshut keah. And yet, those who have separated from lust (like the monks who would retire to deserts where there are no people) have their lust increased even more from seeking lust and not finding it with them, and in everything that is and is found that comes before them, the lust will appear even more intensely:
text.17_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: A fool will not desire wisdom except in the revelation of his heart. There is a difference between a fool and a wretch, for the wretch is one who is content with the laws of wisdom, and in 27 he desires wisdom, for if he could understand everything with wisdom until he was not satisfied, he would desire more. Not so with the fool, who knows the laws of wisdom and is not satisfied. Only desire compels him, and thus he disputes wisdom, and he will not desire wisdom at all, only in the images of desire that are revealed to the heart, because according to the images of his heart that are revealed from the depths of the soul, whether good or evil, he will do, even though he has observed that his images are not good:
text.17_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: When evil comes, also comes contempt, from the measure of justice to honor every person, and the path of wickedness to dishonor, as the saying goes: "And the wicked man will be brought low and disgraced, for all men are despised in his eyes, and if he finds disgrace, he will bring disgrace with him. Disgrace is the reverse of honor, and the path of the wicked is to despise the honorable and to dishonor the lowly with disgrace."
text.17_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: Deep waters are the words of a man's mouth. What a man speaks in words of wisdom is like a deep well, because wisdom is very deep, and originates in the depths of the soul, and from the source to the outlet there is a great distance from depth to surface, and in 27 the source of wisdom is like a stream that flows always without bothering, because wisdom is inherent in the nature of the soul and springs and spreads from the soul. Its springs overflow, only the nature of the body and the desires of the heart deepen and hide it, until the person who wants to speak and offer words of wisdom must tie a rope with a rope, one anointing with another, until he draws the water out of the deep and brings it up to the surface:
text.17_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: It is not good to turn the face of a wicked man against a righteous man in judgment, and the lips of a fool will come into strife, already said that punishing a righteous man is not good, which is the question that is asked in the leadership why Hashem punishes the righteous man, and he said, "The darkness of his words knows knowledge, and the fool keeps silent. A wise man will consider." He illustrated that the fool will be silent and will not ask this question sometimes, because the fool disputes the laws of wisdom because he is satisfied with them and is not wicked because of his desire, and therefore sometimes he will be silent and will not ask these questions about which he has nothing clear, only sufficiency, but the fool knows the laws of wisdom and disputes them because his desire forces him to seek out plots against the wicked, and his lips will come into strife. And he asked both of these questions, about the success of the wicked, asking It is not good to turn the face of a wicked man against a righteous man, why would Hashem turn the face of the wicked man against a righteous man and not punish him, and why did the way of the wicked prosper, and likewise It is not good to turn the face of a righteous man against a righteous man, why would Hashem bring suffering upon the righteous man:
text.17_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: The lips of a fool will come into strife, and his mouth will call for blows. The lips will speak the external word, and the mouth will speak the internal word with wisdom. When the fool asks this question with his external lips, he will already come into strife against Providence, and when he speaks with his mouth and according to the depth of wisdom, he will increase in strife to the point of blows and blows, and he will want to clarify from this that the leadership is against the laws of wisdom:
text.17_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: A fool's mouth is a snare to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul. The snare is the breaking, and the snare is before the snare, and the Lord will make a snare for him with his external lips, in which his soul will be caught in a snare trap, and with his mouth, which is in the inner speech, he will finish the snare with wisdom. With his lips, his soul will be snare to a well of destruction, and what he utters with his mouth will be a snare to his body as well, because Hashem will punish us with bodily punishment as well:
text.17_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: The words of a nagging person are like a nagging person. From this question, a nagging person will arise, who is defined as someone who always complains about Hashem that He created for his harm, and that the evils in the world are greater than the good, and that it is better for him not to have been created, and in this he always complains about Hashem's leadership of His people because they have been left to chance, and his words are like nagging people, as if Hashem were always striking him and doing evil to him, and they descended into the chambers of his stomach, R"l that these evils and blows do not pass him by, but are only in the chambers of his stomach and in his conscience and thoughts, that in his imagination he is always worried and complaining and picturing to himself that everything that his neighbor has is lacking to him, and all the good things of Hashem as if they were evil, as in the parable of the skins that he mentioned in the duty of hearts, and as in the verse instructing that Hashem made man upright, in such a way that the source of evils is in himself and in his imagination, and his words themselves strike and correct him, not blows from without, that if he does not nag him, he will find On the contrary, everything is for the good, and everything is grace and blessing, and he will rejoice in his lot and his soul will rejoice in the salvation of Hashem, for Hashem created man upright and prepared everything for his benefit:
text.17_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: Also, one who is lazy in his work is a brother to a destroyer. Someone who was assigned to do work for the kingdom, and one built the building and destroyed it, and one sat down and did not build at all, the punishment for both is the same, because whether so and so did not build the building assigned to them, and the one who is lazy and did not do it, he is a brother and similar to the owner of the work (R"l who did it) and the destroyer, and likewise there is no difference between someone who performed a mitzvah and committed a transgression that extinguishes a mitzvah and destroys, and between one who sits down and does nothing, neither a mitzvah nor a transgression, for both did not do what was assigned to them. And as it is drawn downward from the greatness of the name of the Lord, the name of the Lord is the tower that people build, and this is their task assigned to them to magnify the name of the Lord and to build His temple, and there is a builder and a destroyer and a non-builder at all, and both are punished the same, and this is also a response for a righteous person and a bad person mentioned above:
text.17_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (10-11) A strong tower is the name of the Lord, rich wealth is the city of his strength. Behold, the name of the Lord is the strong tower in truth, and the righteous who by his righteousness will establish this tower will run in it, for he will do all his deeds in the name of the Lord and for His glory, and will also exalt in it from his spiritual and physical enemies. But the rich will consider his wealth to be Kiryat Ezzo, and it is to him as a lofty wall, and he is found only in his continuity, R"L in the continuance of his heart and his imagination is a lofty wall, but he will not be able to run in this wall nor to excel in it, because it is only an unreal imagination, because the possessions of the world are imaginary possessions and only in the continuity of imagination are their foundation:
text.17_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: Before a break, a man's heart is haughty, he has already said that the abomination of the Lord is every haughty heart, hand to hand, he will not cleanse, R"l that the Lord will punish us immediately, and the haughtiness of the heart is a sign of the break that will follow it, and the rich man who was deceived, in the continuity of his heart like a lofty wall, will be broken, but humility will go before honor, for he who is humble and takes refuge in the tower of strength, the name of the Lord, who dwells in the humble and lowly in spirit, will merit honor:
text.17_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: Answering something before he hears it is a curse for him and a curse, from the path of wisdom that he should not only answer something clear, as in the saying, "Say to wisdom, my sister, if the matter is clear to you as your sister", etc. Therefore, one must hear the questioner's argument and all its sides and decide the clear thing, and in this he will gain respect from the listener. But if an answering before he hears all sides of doubt, he will answer a curse, that is, doubt, and will gain a curse from the listener:
text.17_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's spirit will sustain his illness, the spirit is what carries the body, and even if a sick person is in the body, the spirit's power is great to sustain the illness, and it will give him strength to suffer and to find courage, but if the spirit is afflicted and he is sick in spirit, who will bear it? Then the illness will also affect the body, as the saying goes, and a afflicted spirit will dry up the grain:
text.17_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: A wise heart will acquire knowledge, and the ears of the wise will seek knowledge. The wise man has received the laws of wisdom in Kabbalah and does not have clear knowledge of them, because there is no example for the laws of wisdom. He will only seek knowledge with his ears, he will go to the wise to hear from them the reasons for the laws of wisdom in Kabbalah. However, the wise man who understands a thing from a thing, he will acquire knowledge through his heart, which understands a thing from a thing, and knowledge is his property and he should seek it from others:
text.17_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: "A man who gives will be extended to him - There is a difference between the generous and the generous man, in that the generous man is known to give gifts even to the rich and the great, and although he may seem to be scattering his money freely, sometimes he will be extended to him, because they will be pleased with him before the great, and when he is in need, they will remember his gifts and strive on his behalf.
text.17_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: (17-19) The first righteous man in his dispute, etc. The states decide by lot, etc. A brother who has transgressed, etc., comes to teach that one should not become too strong in a dispute, because the loss is greater than the reward, and it is better for him to compromise, and according to the matter in dispute, they will cast lots between them and according to the lot, so it will be. He said, If you want to argue and think that you will be justified by the judge, here is truly The first righteous man in his dispute, but did not his opponent come and question, and you did not know what he would allege against you and how he would refute your claims, therefore it is good that The states decide by lot. If there is doubt among you and in a dispute and judgment who will take this part and who that part, you sit by lot, and also between great ones, because the Lord thinks that his claims are great and that justice is on his side, lot will separate, but if you want to come specifically For the law, There is a brother who has transgressed from Kiryat Az, R"l There is someone who deserves a share of the inheritance, and he believes he is sure of his right as Kiryat Az, as in the saying, "A rich fortune is Kiryat Az," and he is a transgressor from Kiryat Az, R"l Who has transgressed against him and is taking him out of his inheritance, And judges and the laws close against him Like the lock of a palace that closes tightly and does not allow anyone to enter, because by the judgment and the law it is even more difficult for him to achieve his desire and to enter the city from which he has transgressed, and therefore it is better to make an end by lot, as in the saying, "In the lap of the lot is cast, and from the Lord all his judgment":
text.17_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's mouth will satisfy his stomach, the fruit of his lips will satisfy him. We have already explained that the mouth alludes to speech with wisdom, and the tongue will allude to knowledge. Wisdom, when he speaks it with his mouth, will produce its fruit until his stomach is satisfied, and the fruit is the final fruit and will recommend knowledge. Then he will know the laws of wisdom with clear knowledge until he produces it with his lips, which is the external speech, which is the fruit of the fruit. Then he will be satisfied again with the fruit of knowledge, and behold, wisdom and knowledge will eat and be satisfied. And when he is satisfied, he will eat more, because they are acceptable things. And from the ears of the wise, ask for knowledge as above, and when he receives, he will be satisfied, confirming that he received and will not eat more, but alas.
text.17_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: Death and life are in the hand of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit. The tongue alludes to the sublime, intelligent speech that speaks in the depths of reason, in which it will understand to bring out a word of speech, and in which it will judge between truth and falsehood, on which death and life depend, that the one who believes in the principles of faith through the depths of reason will live, and the one who walks a stubborn path and denies the reality of Hashem and providence and reward and punishment will die, and this depends on the hand of the tongue, which it understood, and those who love it will eat its fruit. He will never be satisfied, but will always eat, because understanding has no limit and will always continue to bring out a word of speech:
text.17_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: He finds a wife, he who finds a wife and finds good and obtains pleasure, meaning he finds a good wife on his part, and also obtains pleasure on the part of the woman, who desires him, and he obtains good from her, this is Ma, by Hashem's providence and goodness:
text.17_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: The rich man will speak supplications, if the rich man speaks supplications and begs, then the rich man will answer and subdue the strong, even if he is strong by nature, his nature will subdue to fulfill the rich man's supplications:
text.17_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: A man of evil, the scholars have already said that the one who loves many does not even have one, because love is one, and whatever is multiplied is useless and separates, and whoever has many evil friends, he only associates so that he may pretend to be a man of evil and evil, because this is a fence of building, marvel at the appearance, and in reality he has no enemies, and there is a lover if he has one lover then he is adherent to a brother, and this is the fence of love, which will grow above all loves even from brotherly love:
text.18_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: It is better to be wise, better to be wise until everyone sees his external wisdom, but he walks in his integrity, unwavering in his righteousness and his heart is right, because he has inner spiritual wealth, than someone who is a fool in his inwardness, whose lust rules over him and deprives him of the wealth of wisdom, and he is wise in his inwardness, and he is stubborn with his lips and hides what is in his heart, and with his lips he insists on his inner way as if he loves wisdom. R"l is wise in body and rich in soul than the opposite:
text.18_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: Even if he does not stray from the path through foolishness, only through lack of knowledge, because his soul is without knowledge, it is also not good. Even if he hastens with his feet out of habit and thus strays from the path, he is also a sinner:
text.18_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's path will be crooked, his way and his heart will be angry with the Lord. The Lord prepared man in such a way that he would be able to walk in the way of goodness and life, through the laws of wisdom that He revealed to him, and since he believes in the laws of wisdom, he will walk in the way of goodness and will not be angry with the Lord for not creating a straight path. Only his path and his lack of understanding in the ways of wisdom will cause his path to be crooked, and this path is not attributed to the Lord because it is the path of man on the part of man, and he will be angry with the Lord for not creating him properly and not showing him the good and straight path:
text.18_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: Wealth will add many enemies If you see that the rich have many enemies, they are not the enemies of the rich, only of the wealth that he will add many enemies, as he adds money, so will his friend, and the poor as he parted with his wealth, so will his friend, because most of the enemies and love are the love of oneself, and depend on the wealth that is expected to benefit from it:
text.18_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: A witness to lies. There is a difference between a lie and a falsehood, since a lie is obvious to all and a falsehood appears true at first, and there is a difference between a witness and a liar, since a witness testifies in accordance with the law of complete testimony, and a liar is a weak word, such as one who utters with his lips. He said, "He who testifies in an obvious lie will certainly not be exempt from punishment, and even if he only utters with his lips, not in accordance with the law of testimony, and he also utters falsehoods that appear true at first, 27 he will not escape because in the end he will be revealed as a liar and will be punished:
text.18_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: "Many will welcome the face of a generous person, and all evil will befall the giver - The definition of a generous person is one who gives as is appropriate at the appropriate time to the appropriate person, as to the poor in his time of need. And the giver always distributes, and also to the rich, due to the degree of extravagance.
text.18_Chapter, 5_Verse, 1_Comment: The generous person has no enemies, because the rich will not be afraid of him because he does not give them gifts. Only many will be pleased with him, who are the poor and the needy, and only many will be pleased, not all, I mean, poor and not rich.
text.18_Chapter, 5_Verse, 2_Comment: But to a man of giving, everyone is his enemy, poor and rich, and they will also associate with him through flattery, because flattery depends on one's own pleasure, and is not true flattery, as in verse 4.
text.18_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: <b>All of Resh's brothers hated him, even though they distanced themselves from his companion, saying, "What are they?" However, Resh is more than the poor, for the poor will only separate from his companion. <b>And Resh's brothers also hated him, and as for his companion, his enemies certainly hated him because they had already distanced themselves from him. If his close brothers hated him, how much more so did the enemies of those who were far away. And in 27 he was a pursuer, saying, "What are they?" And he said, "They are his, that they belong to him, and they are his friends and lovers."
text.18_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: A heart that loves its own soul is bought. The heart indicates the power of the ruler within a person, and even he who knows the laws of wisdom still does not have his own heart, because desire and wisdom are at war in his heart, and the instinct builds great fortresses within it to conquer the heart under its rule. And he who loves his soul and wants to preserve it from being cut off by the enemy, he buys the heart, as the saying goes.
text.18_Chapter, 7_Verse, 1_Comment: * (14:33) Wisdom will rest in a wise heart, for by contemplating the ways of wisdom with the power of reason, he will understand its reasons, the war will cease and the heart will be in his possession, and this is called buying, because wisdom is like money with which one buys goods, as in the saying, "Buying wisdom is chosen from money, and with this money one buys the heart that will be his own," and it is interpreted that this is by keeping wisdom, and since sometimes one will seek evil through his understanding, and will understand in false ways and find false opinions, it is said with the condition that one keeps wisdom in order to find good, and it is interpreted that.
text.18_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: A witness to lies will not be acquitted. If he observes and brings out a false thing, because the intellect discerns between truth and falsehood, and bears false witness, such as denying the reality of Hashem or His providence, he will not be acquitted from punishment, and even if he produces falsehoods by misleading assertions, since the lie is not immediately apparent only after examination and examination, he will perish, and in this there is no duplication with what already came in this verse above, verse 5:
text.18_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: Pleasure is not pleasing to the fool. The fool knows the laws of wisdom, but lust has overcome him, wanting pleasure and the pleasures of the world, and this pleasure is not pleasing to him, because although the body may enjoy pleasure, the soul will eventually submit to the lust of the body, and it is not fitting that the body should rule over the soul, and it will submit to the body that was created to be its slave and will remain in its own power. And from this itself he knows that it is not pleasing for the slave to rule over the flesh, because for this reason pleasure is not pleasing to the fool, because the slave body rules over the soul:
text.18_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's mind is long-suffering. From the ways of reason and understanding, he will not immediately take revenge, but will only prolong his anger, as the saying goes: A man who is long-suffering is wise, and a man of understanding will keep silent, and a man who is short-suffering will make a fool of himself. And this a man's mind, R"t. This requires a man's simple mind, because if he wants to take revenge, even his friend will cheer for him and despise him, but he should completely overlook the crime and not harbor hatred in his heart. This is the law of wisdom, and this is the glory of man, since he is religious, and the wisdom of Hashem, and he has good sense in his heart to boast:
text.18_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: A king's wrath is like a kuffar's wrath. When the king is in wrath and sorrow, no one can approach him, like the kuffar when he is in wrath, for the kuffar does not go out on his prey, but devours all who approach his tent. But in time of desire, then it is like dew on grass, which moistens the grass and infuses life into each grass, and each grass in itself, so the dew of salvation will fall around him on all his servants, and all will draw near to the light of his face, and see above.
text.18_Chapter, 11_Verse, 1_Comment: * (16:14) The wrath of the king of the angels of death:
text.18_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: He was a foolish son to his father and a treacherous womanizer, as already said above.
text.18_Chapter, 12_Verse, 1_Comment: * (18:25) The son of a fool was angry with his father, and here he said that if a woman's affairs are taken to the son of a fool, then the affairs in the house are like a leak that leaks through the roof into the house and ruins the house. If he leaves the house and finds his son a fool and his evil deeds, then it will be death and ruin for his father, for through the fool the affairs will always be added until he is ruined:
text.18_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: House and wealth are the inheritance of ancestors. The house and wealth will be inherited from fathers to sons. It is inherited from the father and will be passed on to his sons after him, on the condition that if Hashem gives him a wise wife who will succeed her husband and manage the house and wealth wisely, then the inheritance will remain for generations, because the woman is the guardian of the wealth, and she is the one who destroys the house with her hands, as the saying goes: A capable woman built her house, but her hands will destroy it.
text.18_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: Laziness brings sleep, he has already praised diligence several times, and in contrast to diligence he condemned laziness and deceit, and here he said that deceit is worse than laziness, that the lazy person will not starve because laziness brings sleep, and if he falls into a deep sleep he will not need to eat, but deceit, that if he does not obtain his need and he does not sleep, his soul will starve:
text.18_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: He who keeps a mitzvah guards his soul. Before a person there are two paths, the path of life and the path of death, and Hashem knows which path he will take, because there is a straight path before a person, and at the end of it are the paths of death. One must listen to a mitzvah that commands him which path he will take and live, and then he guards his soul. But he who despises his ways and walks in the ways of his heart and the desires of the despised, will die the death of the soul:
text.18_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: The Lord lends to the poor, and his reward will be paid to him. Whoever gives a free gift to the poor with grace is like lending to the Lord, who, in addition to paying the debt, will also pay the reward, since the reward is the admiration of love that will also be paid by the love that surrounded him in his goodness, which is greater than the debt itself (and the Lord lends to the poor, R.L. What the rich have is borrowed from the Lord so that he may be generous to the poor, and with this he will pay the reward to the Lord for the loan):
text.18_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: Chastise your son because there is hope, do not think that there is no hope and that your son has already gone out into a bad culture, and from that, refrain from chastising him, saying that there is hope, and likewise do not refrain from chastising him because he is troubled and crying, do not burden yourself with this either:
text.18_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: He who grows angry bears punishment. The punishment bears the punishment of the one who grows angry. If he is a man who grows angry and angry, he will bear the punishment. By the punishment you punish him, his anger will be appeased. But if you save and do not punish him, the anger will increase even more. And you should discipline your son and do not think that he has no cure because there is hope, and do not bear your soul thinking death of the death of the soul because there is no cure for him. He grows anger The growth that the child will grow on me, butter (L. in the bath of my steps in the heat), the fruit that this growth bears is a punishment, but if you save and empty this fruit, R"L if you wish to remove the punishment, you will add its fruit, and the punishment will increase even more:
text.18_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: Listen to advice, if you wish to gain wisdom, you should listen to advice, as the saying goes: "And listen to the advice of a wise man, and receive discipline." Advice is according to the ways of wisdom, and discipline is from the fear of Hashem and His punishment, and in this you will become wise in the end, and I have already clarified that the latter is about the purpose and the happiness that comes in the latter, that you will know wisdom for the matter that is beneficial to the latter and the final happiness:
text.18_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: Many thoughts in a person's heart, thoughts are what a person thinks about from every possible angle to reach some goal, and they are many, and they are in a person's heart, because he has the choice to choose one from every possible angle, but in this he will not reach the advice that is the correct way that achieves the goal of his desire, and the advice is diligent from Hashem according to His will, and it will be established, because although the choice is in the hand of man, the finality of the deed is under providence, and in general matters on which Hashem's advice will appear, providence will arise and nullify the choice, as it is said in Makkah:
text.18_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: A man's signs are his kindness, the kindness that a man does is what will define him and describe his character, whose inner form is evident by the kindness that will be revealed from him, according to which his dimensions and nature will be recognized, but a false man, who promises kindness and does not do it, is better than him, for it may be that the nature of his soul is inclined to kindness, but the man is clearly false not only because he cannot be shown kindness, but also because he is lying in his belief:
text.18_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: The fear of Hashem is for life and long life, and no evil will befall him. There is a difference between the fear of Hashem and other fears, because fear of the events of the world shortens life, fear will prevent food and sleep, but the fear of Hashem is for life and long life, so that he may eat to his satisfaction and also sleep, because this fear will remove all other fears from him, because the fear of Hashem is certain that no evil will befall him, and no evil will touch him, and therefore he is confident and has no fear of anything, and therefore the fear of Hashem will add days, as above:
text.18_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: The lazy man buries his hand in the plate, and will not bring it back to his mouth, drawing, meaning: The lazy man's desire is to be satisfied because his hands are too weak to do anything, the lazy man's hand is too weak to move, and if the desire of hunger forces him and he reaches for the plate to take food, he buries his hand there to be safe from the urge to move it, and he is afraid to move it from there, and there it will remain, and he will not bring it back to his mouth, and he will be hungry and will not move his hand:
text.18_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: (27-28-27) A liar will be beaten, etc., a father who robs, etc., his son will cease to hear, etc.. Behold, the fool will not return to observe through the rebuke of reason, only through discipline and beating. If he sees that the liar is being punished, he will acquire cunning to understand, so that he will not follow the path of the liar. But the wise man will show him the discipline of the liar, because through the rebuke of reason he will understand knowledge, because he will be seen to say, "Isn't a son disgraceful and disgraceful to his father and mother with his actions, robbing the father and driving the mother away?" And this is enough rebuke for the wise man, so that he does not do this to his children. And you, my wise son, have ceased to hear discipline. You will not have to hear the discipline of the liar because you have misunderstood the sayings of knowledge, because when you take to heart the sayings of wisdom, The mind, which is clarified by the sense of how the son shamefully robs his parents, will already take this to heart, and turn away from their actions:
text.18_Chapter, 27_Verse, 0_Comment: (28-29) A worthless witness will bring judgment, judges will be prepared for mockers. If you see how a worthless witness who bears false witness mocks judgment, because a judgment is issued to kill a soul without right, like the act of Danboth the Jezreelite, and the mouths of the wicked judges cover the violence, know that there is a judgment and an accounting, Judges will be prepared for mockers, and the wicked will be prepared for blows, false witnesses will judge to do to them as they have planned, and the judges will be punished with blows from heaven:
text.19_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: (Proverbs 21): The wine-drinker - The drinker is one who makes fun of the laws of wisdom, because the laws of wisdom must be accepted with faith and sincerity of heart, otherwise there is no example for them, and teaches that even someone who has accepted the laws of wisdom, if he mistakes with wine - will not be wise, because wine is a drinker, making fun of the laws of wisdom, since it will rule the heart and its desires to deviate from the path of wisdom into debauchery, and everything seems to him to be a plain thing.
text.19_Chapter, 0_Verse, 1_Comment: And here, the joker only jokes about wisdom, not about reason; but the stupid reward does not joke about reason at all, only about brute force, because then his mind is already useless and he becomes like brute animals without reason.
text.19_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: A snarl like a kuffar is a king's terror, he has already said (19:12) A snarl like a kuffar is a king's wrath, that when he is in a rage, one should not approach him like a kuffar in his dwelling during his hunger, for then he will certainly devour, and here he said that even in a time of desire, when one can approach him, one must beware of the king's terror. The boundary of terror is something that is threatened by his great exaltation and virtue, and one must not transgress the laws of terror, for terror will warn that one should not be careless, nor should one use his scepter, and that one should be careful of his appearance, and whoever transgresses these laws is liable to death and sins against his soul, and whoever approaches this terror without feeling it, is as if approaching a kuffar in his dwelling:
text.19_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: Honor to a man of the Sabbath from quarreling. Whoever comes to quarrel because he has been provoked, will not consider him honorable, whether in that by quarreling he will be provoked even more and the purpose will not be achieved, or in that it is he himself who is careful about the slander, a lesson that is in the actual slander, and more he will have honor if he sits away from quarreling, or in that which shows that he is not careful, as in the saying, "A bondman is a double-minded man," or in that which protects him from disgrace, as in the saying, "Do not go out to quarrel hastily, lest what will you do in the end?" etc., and this is the law of wisdom to restrain his anger, but the fool who is content with the law of wisdom will not be able to restrain his spirit, and his lesser qualities are revealed immediately, as in the saying, "Woe to the day that knows his anger" (12:16):
text.19_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: A lazy person will not plow and ask at the harvest and there is none. The time for plowing is in winter and then the weather is cold, and the lazy person who does not like to do work even at the right time, when he is lazy in the winter solstice, and then when the harvest comes when the weather is good asks to eat and there is none, and he is a parable about the man who is lazy to gather wisdom in his youth, when it is time to plow the plot of the soul from the thorns and briers and the images of desire, and to sow in it the seed of wisdom and knowledge, but then the boiling of choices and his desires will prevent him from doing so and he will be lazy, and then in his old age when the boiling of childhood has subsided, but since he did not prepare the soil of the soul for wisdom in its time, he will not find fruit. Similarly, winter will recommend the days of the soul's life in the body, when it is time for plowing and sowing, and when the soul sheds its material clothing, then it is time for harvesting, and whoever did not bother In the name of what one should eat on Shabbat:
text.19_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: Deep waters are counsel in the heart of a man, and a man of understanding will guide him. Counsel is to choose the best and most beneficial of all possible parts, and behold, many thoughts flow like a stream of water across the heart, as it is said, “Many thoughts are in the heart of a man.” But the counsel, which is to choose the best of all possible parts, leading to the desired goal, is hidden deep in the heart, at the source of the north, in the depths of a great abyss. There is counsel according to wisdom, and this is the counsel of Hashem, who instilled the laws of wisdom, and he received this counsel from others, because wisdom is acceptable among men. And a wise man listens to counsel, for the law of a priest and counsel from a wise man will not perish. (Jeremiah 18:18) Indeed, the counsel that is in the heart of man himself, to understand with his mind to choose the good, is very deep, and will not be diminished from the depths of the soul only by the power of the intellect, which understands one thing from another, and judges with the power of his intellect all the parts of the contradictory, to see from all the multitude of thoughts which is the best of all, and the investigation of the intellect by reasoning is like a well of water. From a deep place, one ties rope to rope until one descends to the well, and so one ties a string to a string until one brings out the truth through the power of understanding:
text.19_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: A great man will be called a man of kindness Kindness is what he does not out of obligation or promise, but out of a generous heart, and faith is what he does out of obligation or promise, and as such it would be fitting that someone who does kindness should do so out of faith, that if he volunteers what he did not commit to, he will keep the obligation and what is incumbent upon him. Indeed, in human nature, it would appear to be the opposite, that few people of faith will do what is incumbent upon them lightly, they will be deceived and will touch the wealth of others. However, when it comes before them to do kindness, many will find it to do it, and this is because people do not do good for themselves only for the glory and praise, and they will be even more delighted if they do kindness, because in this their kindness will be declared, and this is the reason why A great man will be called a man of kindness. With this, many will find it to do kindness, so that each and every one will call out his kindness and make it public, although No faithful person will be found, because from this no honor will be bestowed. And glory, and also R.L. Who will find a faithful man who will do true kindness, which is kindness done in modesty, not with much proclamation and publicity, because the root of every deed is the love of honor and retribution:
text.19_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: The righteous man walks in his integrity, blessed are his children after him. The righteous man is one who does the work of righteousness and is not yet perfect, because the boundary of innocence is that he does all his deeds for the name of Hashem alone, not for the sake of honor, glory, and external appearance, for then he will not always stand by his righteousness, and who will be drawn to the word of Hashem? A faithful man, who will be found? And so the righteous man is not perfect in acting in faith. However, the righteous man who walks in his integrity, doing all his deeds for the sake of Hashem (and Hashem walks in a way that preserves the steadfastness that the righteous will never err), even though he may not attain the apparent praise, Blessed are his children after him, because the reward of innocence (who did not want to enjoy the reward of his deeds) will remain for his children from generation to generation:
text.19_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: (8-9) A king sits on a throne of judgment, who can say, "I have earned my heart?" The wise man has already said, "If you see oppression and plunder in the land, do not be surprised at the object, for He is higher than the highest, and there is no justice in the land, know that the reason for this is because the highest judge in the land does not oversee justice himself, he only delegates the administration of justice to the deputy minister under him, and the minister delegates it to the one under him, and the oppressed will not be able to reach the king himself for justice. For then it will be shown that the lesser judges will not oversee justice, or they have no power or they will follow greed and bribery. Indeed, if the king himself sits on a throne of judgment, and executes justice himself, then he will certainly execute justice for the oppressed, and the arm of a high priest will be broken." He said about this four conditions: a) That the king executes justice himself, b) That he sits on a throne of judgment, Sitting on the throne indicates the determination, 3] that he sits on the throne of judgment, that there is a difference between a throne of judgment and a court of law, that the judgment is the final judgment and the ruling, and the judgment is the hearing of the arguments of the judge, who will also hear the arguments of the judge himself, not through the lawyers of the judges and judges who hear the arguments, who will thereby be able to mislead the Supreme Judge, 4] <He removes all evil from his eyes, who, apart from the judgment, watches over the people in a great way and scatters and scatters evil with the eyes of his supervision, that he himself walks among the people to watch over evildoers to cut off all workers of iniquity, when all these conditions are present Who would say, "I have justified my heart," and how would it seem to a man that if he is justified in his heart, he would already be purified from his sin? Would he not fear and be afraid of this great judge who has absolute power, and who is not swayed by bribery, and 27 a parable about the great and awesome King, the Lord Hashem, on whom he sits Always on the throne of judgment, and with His eyes watching all the actions of men with His constant personal supervision, and who would not fear this judge, whether for the thoughts of his heart, for who would say, "I have justified my heart." Or for his actual actions, for "I have been cleansed from my sin," and for example:
text.19_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: A stone and a stone anywhere and everywhere. Let something be depicted that is bad according to the manifest and not bad according to the observed, such as if the buyer of a stone and a stone must weigh the meathe, in a large weight and a small weight, and the seller must measure the fruits according to this value, so that if the seller sells in a small amount, he pays the meathe in the small weight, although in this he can say, "I have gained my heart," since he gives according to justice, 27 he cannot say, "I have been cleansed from my sin" according to the manifest, because both of them are an abomination to Hashem, even if both of them are found opposite each other, the stone is opposite the ipha, because the Torah generally warned that one should not find a stone and a stone in your pocket in any way and with any justification:
text.19_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: Even in his deeds, a boy will be distinguished whether he acted righteously or not. There is a difference between an action and a deed. Deeds are actions that depend on mental qualities, such as actions that grow from the nature of pride or humility, cruelty or mercy, and so on. He said, "If you see an action or a business from a boy, and you do not know how he did it, and you want to know from this the essence of the boy and his future destiny, you will be able to recognize it by his qualities and standards. For example, Moses killed the Egyptian and said to the wicked man, "Why do you strike your neighbor?" And it is still not known whether he did it out of love of justice and righteousness or out of the nature of revenge and pride, and so on. He went ahead and told his deeds. Moses grew up and went out to his brothers and saw their suffering, which was his deeds and mental qualities.
